## 2026-10-10 — PR: claude/pile-graphics (PR link added after merge)

### F14. New graphics: soil profile beside the pile, p-y curves (Figure F-3), pile cross-sections; Soil profile input tab   [UI only] [no calculation change]
- **Date:** 2026-10-10. **Type:** UI only (presentation). Engineer's decision 2026-10-10: "Do 1, 3, 5" (soil profile beside the pile, p-y curves, pile cross-sections), and the addition the same day: "Can we make the soil profile its own input tab rather than buried inside of a tab." Two commits: (a) the graphics, (b) the input tab (see "F14, part b" below).
- **What changed, part a (graphics):**
  - **Soil profile & pile elevation** (`SoilPileProfile`, static SVG). A boring-log column of the tool's own soil layers (`I.soilLayers`, sorted by top depth), coloured and hatched by the layer `type` (sand / soft clay / stiff clay / weak rock; the tool has no "fill" type), with depth ticks below grade and the pile drawn to the same depth scale beside it (widths schematic). Each layer has a label (leader line, collision-free stack): number, type, top–bottom depth, the p-y model and static/cyclic, and only the values the tool reads, with the solver's own defaults (`ly.gamma || 120` etc.): sand γ, φ, k; clay γ, sᵤ, ε₅₀; weak rock qᵤ, Eₘ, RQD; H-pile adds the static axial values (N̄1₆₀ or Sᵤ and α, "0 (not entered)" when blank, as `hpileGeoCapacity` reads them); the linear basis with layered soil adds n_h / k_h. Hover (SVG `<title>`) shows the full layer values on screen. No groundwater level is an input of this tool, so none is drawn (note under the figure).
    - Micropile: cap, cap embedment, casing (head → casing tip), plunge zone, grouted bond zone (hole d_h), bar, pile head / top of bond / casing tip / toe marks, dimension lines L_cased, plunge, L_b,eff, L_bond and stickup, and the bond value β and d_h (one value for the bond zone, not per layer). Depths below grade are the tool's head-datum depths minus the stickup (`I.solverFree`), the datum the p-y solver uses. With "Buckling" on, the unsupported depth below grade where the solver removes the soil springs (`pyRes.setup.unsupBelowGrade_in`) is hatched "no p-y springs (L_u)".
    - H-pile: cap, cap embedment, section to the embedded length below grade (`I.solverLembed`, as the input and Module G define it), stickup and L_embed dimensions. Where the p-y model's pile ends at a different depth (see O25) a red dashed "p-y model toe" mark is drawn.
    - Integral abutment: abutment cap, 2 ft embedment, 3 ft crushed-stone trench, pile to the required length, L_f line, Tier 2 scour band; soil column = the MassDOT soil type (Simplified Method), plus a second column of the project layers when Tier 2 uses the layered profile.
    - Placed in **Module G** (Geometry & limits tab) in place of the old Plotly `PileElevation` in all three modes (the `PileElevation` function is kept, no longer referenced). The old micropile elevation drew the casing tip and toe at their head-datum depths below grade, i.e. 3 ft too deep at the default 3 ft stickup; the new drawing uses the solver's datum. Module G's grid column is widened (`pd-geom-grid`, 560 px from 1280 px up).
  - **Figure F-3: p-y curves at selected depths** (`PyCurvesFig`, `PyCurvesChart`, static SVG + table). A figure card on the **Lateral (p-y)** tab after Module 02 (CSS order 21).
    - Nonlinear p-y basis: the curves are evaluated with the solver's own objects. The `pyRes` memo now also returns `pNode: res2.p` (the solver's nodal soil reactions) and `setup: { soilAt, stick_in, L_in, D, soilTop_in, unsupBelowGrade_in, nNodes, gPM, gYM }` (the soil records with their Georgiadis offsets, datum and multipliers the solve used). Nothing else in the memo changes and nothing reads these fields except the figure. Each curve is `|pyPofY(model, y, z, prm, f_m, f_y)|` at the solver node nearest the requested depth; the mobilised point is the solver's nodal y (`pyRes.records[i].defl`) and nodal p (`pyRes.pNode[i]`). The table lists depth, model + static/cyclic (cyclic applies to sand and soft clay only; the tool has no cyclic stiff-clay or weak-rock form), width b (d_h below the casing tip where entered), Georgiadis z_e, f_m·p_u, y, p, p/p_u and |p − p(y)|. f_m = `I.pyPM` and f_y = `I.pyYM` are applied exactly as the solver applies them; group row factors reach the solver only through f_m ("Apply avg fm"), which the note states.
    - Default depths: mid-depth of each layer between the top of the springs and the depth where |M| decays to 5 % of M_max (`pyRes.zMomentDecay`), the head region (one pile width below the top of the springs) and the depth of M_max; at most 8 curves. The engineer can remove depths (chip ×) and add depths; a user list is remembered per browser in the **new key `micropile_lrfd_pyCurveDepths_v1`** (array of ft below grade; removed = automatic). Not in project data.
    - Linear (Winkler) basis: the straight springs p = E_s·y with E_s from the solver's `subgradeAt()` and the linear solution's deflections. "Input Mmax (from LPILE)": a note that the curves are those of the LPILE model (no curves drawn). Integral abutment: no Lateral tab (Tier 2 already plots its own p-y curves).
    - Curves are computed once per solve (memoised on `pyRes` and the depth list), not while typing elsewhere.
  - **Pile cross-sections** (`PileSectionsFig`, static SVG + tables), a card at the top of the **Structural** tab (CSS order 29).
    - Micropile, one scale for both: cased section (nominal OD dashed with the corrosion band hatched, corroded steel ring OD_r–ID hatched, grout core, bar as the tool's equivalent round bar 2√(A_b/π)), dimensions OD and ID, callouts t / t_r, corrosion / OD_r, grout f′c, bar A_b / Ø_eq; uncased bond-zone section (hole d_h, grout, bar). Tables with the tool's computed values only: A_cas, A_g (cased, uncased), A_b, I_cas (`r.comb.Icas`), S_j / Z_j (`r.flex`), EI casing only, EI used by the p-y solver, EI uncased. Centralisers and couplers are not modelled by the tool and are not drawn.
    - H-pile: I-section to scale with b_f and d dimensions, t_f / t_w / h_w callouts, the bending axis used (heavy dash-dot) and the other axis (light); table from `r.hpileStruct.hp` (A_g, A_eff when slender, I, S, Z, r, governing-axis I and S, EI to the p-y solver, p-y bearing width). **The tool has no H-pile corrosion input**, so no corroded outline is drawn; the note says the section and properties are nominal.
  - **Printed report** (each figure in its print-chooser group, default ticked, kept on one page, static SVG): Figure G-1 soil profile in "G" (micropile, H-pile; group Geometry & limits) and in "01b Section & Soil" (integral abutment; group Simplified Method); Figure S-1 cross-sections at the start of "03" (micropile) / "03–09" (H-pile) (group Structural); Figure F-3 in its own block headed "02F" after Figure F-2 (group Lateral). `PrintReport` takes a new `gfx` prop (linear solution, active layers, F-3 depths, EI values). Page counts at the defaults: micropile 9 → 13, H-pile 7 → 9, integral abutment 4 → 5.
- **Not changed:** `computeAll`, `solvePyPile`, `buildPySetup`, every p-y model, every check and every displayed result; storage keys `micropile_lrfd_inputs_v1`, `micropile_lrfd_lpile_v1`, `micropile_lrfd_outTab_v1`, `micropile_lrfd_printSel_v1`, IndexedDB `micropile_lrfd_db`; the saved / exported JSON; `bridgeSuite.v1.projectMeta` and `foundationLoads`; library tags and versions (no new library: plain SVG).
- **New storage key (per browser, UI only, never in project data):** `micropile_lrfd_pyCurveDepths_v1`, read/written in try/catch.
- **Governing provision:** none (presentation only). No formula, factor, unit, default or code reference changed.
- **Check case (p-y curves, independent evaluation):** micropile defaults with layers sand (0–5 ft, γ 120, φ 34°, k 110) / soft clay (5–9 ft, γ 110, sᵤ 600 psf, ε₅₀ 0.02) / stiff clay (9–25 ft, γ 120, sᵤ 2500 psf, ε₅₀ 0.006) / sand (25 ft+, γ 62, φ 38°, k 125), user depths 1, 3, 6, 8, 12, 20 ft. The plotted points (91 per curve, read from the rendered figure's data) were compared with a separate implementation of Reese, Cox & Koop (1974) sand (wedge / flow p_s, A/B factors, parabola, initial k·z line), Matlock (1970) soft clay (static and cyclic) and the tool's Welch & Reese stiff-clay form (Matlock p_u, ½p_u(y/y₅₀)^¼, 16 y₅₀), using the solver's Georgiadis equivalent depth: P_lat = 12 kip, static, f_m = f_y = 1: max relative difference 2.3·10⁻¹⁶; P_lat = 5 kip, cyclic, f_m = 0.70, f_y = 1.20: 3.3·10⁻¹⁶. The mobilised points lie on their curves: |p_solver − p(y)| ≤ 6·10⁻¹⁴ lb/in at every depth (e.g. z = 6.10 ft soft clay, z_e = 7.82 ft: y = 0.9103 in, p = 180.497 lb/in both ways). The Georgiadis offsets themselves were not re-derived.
- **How verified:**
  - `node --check` on all four inline scripts (pre-compiled `React.createElement`; no JSX to transpile).

### F14, part b. Soil profile input tab   [UI only] [no calculation change]
- **Date:** 2026-10-10. Engineer: "Can we make the soil profile its own input tab rather than buried inside of a tab."
- **What changed:**
  - New input-rail tab **"Soil profile"** after Pile (`RAIL_TABS` id `soilprof`). It holds one panel, `SoilProfilePanel` (marked `data-rtab-fixed="soilprof"`, id `pd-soilprof`): the soil profile drawing (`SoilPileProfile`, updates live as layers are edited, hover for values) above the layer inputs, which are the **same component** the Soil Profile Workspace dialog showed (`PyLayerTable`: layer table, add layer, import boring-log JSON, copy AI prompt, H-pile static axial table) and the same "use layered profile" box (`solverLayered`). Every input keeps its key and handler; saved data are unchanged.
  - The tab is shown for micropile and H-pile, and for integral abutment only when Tier 2 is on with the layered soil source (`I.iabTier2 && I.iabNlSoilSource === "layered"`), the only case where that mode reads the layers. Otherwise the tab is not shown in that mode.
  - The old "Soil / p-y" tab keeps the head condition, p-y settings, uniform-soil settings and (micropile) the Geotechnical bond panel; it is renamed **"Bond / p-y"** for micropile and **"p-y / lateral"** for H-pile and integral abutment (`labelFor`).
  - Every button that opened the Soil Profile Workspace dialog now selects the Soil profile tab, scrolls to it and focuses the first editable layer field (`gotoSoilProfileTab`): the "≡ SOIL PROFILE" button and the Geotechnical-panel button in the rail, the Tier 2 button (integral abutment) and the Module 02 button. The three "◈ SOIL PROFILE WORKSPACE" labels now read "◈ SOIL PROFILE → Soil profile tab"; the "≡ SOIL PROFILE" label is unchanged. The dialog itself (`SoilModal`) is no longer opened (kept in the file).
  - The red warning dot works on the new tab (an import with warnings marks it, as before for its old tab). Layer-table inputs in the rail use 11 px text and no spin buttons so values are not cut off.
  - **Tab memory:** the input-rail tab is not stored (it starts on Pile at each load: `useState("pile")`); there is no stored value to migrate. The output-tab key `micropile_lrfd_outTab_v1` is unaffected.
- **Not changed:** any calculation, input key, storage key, saved / exported data or hand-off.
- **Governing provision:** none (presentation only).
- **How verified:** `node --check` on all inline scripts; headless Chromium: parity main vs branch as in part a (defaults and layered profile, all three modes) identical; each of the jump buttons selects the Soil profile tab, shows it and focuses a layer field; an import with warnings puts the red dot on the Soil profile tab; integral abutment without Tier 2 shows no Soil profile tab; localStorage keys after use: only `micropile_lrfd_outTab_v1` and `micropile_lrfd_inputs_v1` (no rail-tab key); screenshots at 1500 and 400 px (no horizontal page scroll); no console errors.
- **Other copies:** none.
- **Re-applying by hand:** unified diff below (CRLF stripped). Hunks: rail CSS (anchor `aside.input-rail[data-rtab-active="phi"]`); `SoilProfilePanel` and `gotoSoilProfileTab` after `GfxRptFig`; the four workspace buttons (anchors `setSoilModalOpen(true)`, `SOIL PROFILE WORKSPACE`); the `SoilProfilePanel` element before the micropile `title: "Geotechnical"` panel; `RAIL_TABS` and `labelFor`.

## 2026-10-10 — PR: claude/pile-loads-tab (PR link added after merge)

### F15. "Loads & group" input tab: single pile or pile group, load cases, group workspace and hand-off in one place   [UI / workflow only] [no calculation change]
- **Date:** 2026-10-10. Engineer: "I think the pile group workspace and loading should be a new input tab. It should allow for a single pile and manual entry of loading as well as the pile group."
- **What changed:**
  - New input-rail tab **"Loads & group"** (`RAIL_TABS` id `loads`), after Soil profile and before Bond / p-y (lateral) — the order is now Project, Pile, Soil profile, **Loads & group**, Bond / p-y, Cap, Checks, φ: what the pile is, what it sits in and what it carries come first, then the analysis settings and checks. One rail block, `LoadsGroupPanel` (`data-rtab-fixed="loads"`, id `pd-loads`):
    1. **"Single pile or pile group"**: two radio cards, *Single pile — enter loads manually* and *Pile group — cap loads distributed to the piles*. Under them, **"Foundation loads from another tool"**: the "Pull from Abutment / SubLoads" (● new data) and "Import hand-off (JSON)" buttons and the source line, moved here from the Project Info panel with the same ids (`pfxPull`, `pfxNew`, `pfxImp`, `pfxFile`, `pfxSrc`) and handlers. They serve both modes because the import dialog itself asks for the target (group workspace by default, or the single-pile case table); the dialog is unchanged.
    2. **Pile group only — "Pile group workspace"**: the content of the Pile Group Workspace dialog, now `GroupWorkspaceBody` (shared by the tab, one column, and the dialog, two columns as before; every input, key and handler is the dialog's). In the tab it starts with **"Plan & per-pile forces"** (`GroupLayoutView`): a to-scale SVG plan (`GroupPlanSvg`: cap outline, stem, piles numbered P1…, axial under each pile, design pile ringed, load locations, group centroid, dimension chains in ft for the pile centre lines and the overall cap) and the per-pile table (x, y, axial, shear) for one group case — the active case when it is a Group ▦ row, otherwise the first non-zero group case; a selector shows any other case without changing the active case. Then 1 Pile layout, 2 Load locations, 2b Load cases × magnitudes, 2b Cap geometry & self-weight, the edge-distance check, 3 Design pile, the 3D view behind a "Show 3D view" button, max compression / uplift / shear, and "Make the Group ▦ case the ACTIVE load case" (was in the dialog footer).
    3. **"LRFD load cases (per pile)"** (single pile) or **"Design load cases (per pile)"** (pile group: your rows + the computed Group ▦ rows): `LoadCasesCard` with the new `variant: "edit"` — svc defl limit, Run all cases → envelope, active-case selector, editable rows (add / delete / rename / type), the computed Group ▦ rows read-only as before. After "Run all" it shows "Envelope: n cases run · k not satisfied — results on the Summary tab →".
  - **How the mode is determined (no migration, no new field):** the choice *is* the existing input `I.groupEnable` ("Apply pile group to the design" in the dialog, "Evaluate group effects" in Module 11): Single pile = `false`, Pile group = `true`. Every saved project therefore opens in the mode that reproduces its results. Choosing Single pile writes `groupEnable: false, loadFromGroup: false`, choosing Pile group writes `groupEnable: true` — exactly what the dialog's checkbox wrote. Nothing is deleted when switching: the group layout, load locations, group cases and cap inputs stay in the inputs (not applied in single-pile mode, as before); the manual load cases are applied in both modes (as before, group mode adds the Group ▦ rows to them).
  - **Summary output tab:** `LoadCasesCard` `variant: "summary"` (id `pd-cases-sum`): read-only case table (◉ buttons still switch the active case), the active-case selector, svc defl limit (as text), Run all cases → envelope, **Edit loads →**, and the envelope results table and moment-profile plot (moved out of the input card).
  - **Jumps to the new tab** (`gotoLoadsTab`): Summary "Edit loads →" and the Loads panel (Checks tab) "Edit loads →" (focus the first case field); the "▦ PILE GROUP → Loads & group tab" button on the Checks tab (was "▦ PILE GROUP WORKSPACE", opened the dialog) and the new link in Module 11's note (focus the workspace); Project Info "Loads & group tab →". The dialog (`GroupModal`) is no longer opened (kept in the file).
  - **Text that pointed at the old places** now names the tab: Loads panel sub and note, Uplift panel sub, Group options note, Module 02 note ("left column card"), Module 06 cap note, Module 11 note, `CapResults` empty message, `GroupCasesTable` note, the workspace's "main Load Cases section". Project Info sub no longer mentions the hand-off; in integral-abutment mode its body says hand-offs are not used in that mode.
  - **Integral abutment:** the tab is not shown (that mode takes its gravity load in the Abutment panel and has no LRFD case table or group workspace). The hand-off buttons are therefore not shown in that mode; before, they were shown and the import was refused there with a message ("Integral-abutment mode takes the unfactored gravity load per pile …").
  - **Red dot:** works as for every rail tab (a ⚠ inside the tab marks it): e.g. pile group with no cap plan (cap L × W = 0) or a failed "Run all".
  - **Printed report:** content unchanged except **Figure 11-1** (the same `GroupPlanSvg` for `r.capDist`, the distribution the section prints) added at the top of the Group (11) print group, after the resultant lines. Load-case and group tables print as before.
  - CSS: rail hide rule for `loads`, the radio cards (`.pd-mode*`), no spin buttons in the tab's tables, a wider name and type column in the case table.
- **Not changed:** `computeAll`, `computeCapDist`, the Group ▦ case emission, `runAllCases`, every check and status; every input key and the saved / exported / autosaved data (no new field); storage keys (`micropile_lrfd_inputs_v1`, `micropile_lrfd_lpile_v1`, `micropile_lrfd_outTab_v1`, `micropile_lrfd_printSel_v1`, IndexedDB `micropile_lrfd_db`); the `foundationLoads` receiver code and dialog, and the `projectMeta` share; library tags.
- **Governing provision:** none (presentation / workflow only). No formula, factor, unit, default or code reference changed.
- **Check case:** not applicable (no result changes). Parity: see How verified.
- **How verified:**
  - `node --check` on all four inline scripts (pre-compiled `React.createElement`; no JSX).
  - Headless Chromium, pinned libraries served locally, origin/main vs branch, after "Run all cases" with every module expanded: (a) defaults in all three modes; (b) a single-pile project with 4 manual cases (strength / extreme / service / tension, active = Ext I, svc limit 0.75 in) in micropile and H-pile; (c) a group project (2 × 3 piles at 4 ft, cap 12 × 8 × 3 ft with self-weight, two load locations, eccentric cap loads, 2 group cases Str I / Ext I, plus one manual case) in micropile and H-pile. Identical: output-column text (the load-case card compared separately, plus the known text changes above), case names, active case, envelope table, report text (figures removed), summary strip, module statuses, autosave JSON, `Save .json` export, localStorage key list. No console errors.
  - A project saved by main (the group project's exported .json, via "Load .json" and via autosave) opens on the branch in Pile group mode with the same summary strip.
  - Hand-off: abutment calculator "Send foundation loads" → Pile Designer pull, main vs branch, target group (default) and target single: new-data marker, dialog text, resulting inputs (timestamps removed), source line and summary strip identical; the group import switches the tab to Pile group, the single import leaves Single pile.
  - Mode switch on the group project: Single pile → `groupEnable` false, `loadFromGroup` false, group cases / load points / pile coordinates / manual cases unchanged, Group ▦ rows gone; back to Pile group → inputs and output text identical to before.
  - Jumps: Summary "Edit loads", Loads panel "Edit loads", the Checks-tab group button, Module 11 link and Project Info link all select the Loads & group tab (and focus a case field / the workspace). Dot: none at the defaults; shown for a group with no cap plan. Integral abutment: tabs Project, Abutment, p-y / lateral. No horizontal page scroll at 400 px in either mode. Screenshots at 1500 and 400 px in both modes, and the printed Figure 11-1 (Letter PDF), looked at.
- **Other copies:** none (all tool-specific).
- **Re-applying by hand:** unified diff below (CRLF stripped). Hunks: rail CSS (anchor `aside.input-rail[data-rtab-active="soilprof"]`); `LoadCasesCard` (variant); `GroupModal` split into `GroupWorkspaceBody` + `GroupModal` (anchor `function GroupModal(`); text in `CapResults`, `GroupCasesTable`, workspace, `PyPanel`; the report's 11 block (anchor `r.capDist.capWt_incl &&`); new `gotoLoadsTab`, `GroupPlanSvg`, `GroupLayoutView`, `LoadsGroupPanel` before `function InteractionDiagram(`; `App`: Project Info panel, the Checks-tab group button, Loads panel, `LoadsGroupPanel` element after `SoilProfilePanel`, Group options / Uplift / cap-geometry / Module 11 text, the Summary `LoadCasesCard`; `RAIL_TABS`.

```diff
@@ -5612,6 +5625,218 @@ function gotoSoilProfileTab(setRailTab) {
     const f = el.querySelector("table input:not([disabled]), table select"); if (f) f.focus({ preventScroll: true });
   }, 60);
 }
+/* ============================================================
+   LOADS & GROUP INPUT TAB (UI only, 2026-10-10)
+   ------------------------------------------------------------
+   One rail tab for the design loads. The choice at the top is the existing
+   input I.groupEnable ("Apply pile group to the design"): Single pile = off,
+   Pile group = on. Nothing new is stored; both sets of data are kept when the
+   choice changes (the group data are just not applied in single-pile mode).
+   Single pile: the LRFD load-case table (LoadCasesCard, variant "edit").
+   Pile group: the Pile Group Workspace content (GroupWorkspaceBody, rail
+   layout) with a dimensioned plan and the per-pile table, then the design
+   case table with its computed Group rows, as before. The foundation-load
+   hand-off buttons sit under the choice (the import dialog itself asks which
+   target). Display-only helpers below call the existing computeCapDist with
+   the same arguments the case table uses; nothing feeds back into a check.
+============================================================ */
+function gotoLoadsTab(setRailTab, part) {
+  setRailTab("loads");
+  setTimeout(() => {
+    const el = document.getElementById(part === "group" ? "pd-grpws" : part === "cases" ? "pd-cases-edit" : "pd-loads") || document.getElementById("pd-loads");
+    if (!el) return;
+    el.scrollIntoView({ block: "start", behavior: "auto" });
+    const f = el.querySelector(part === "cases" ? "table input:not([disabled]), table select" : "input:not([disabled]), select"); if (f) f.focus({ preventScroll: true });
+  }, 60);
+}
+/* Plan of the pile group, to scale (SVG): cap outline, stem, piles numbered as in
+   the tables, axial per pile for the case given (cd = computeCapDist result),
+   design pile ringed, load locations, group centroid, dimension chains (ft). */
+function GroupPlanSvg({ I, cd, print, showAxial = true }) {
+  const e = React.createElement;
+  if (!cd || !cd.piles || !cd.piles.length) return null;
+  const piles = cd.piles, n = piles.length;
+  const D = Math.max((pileWidth(I) || 0) / 12, 0.05);
+  const capOn = I.capL > 0 && I.capW > 0;
+  const ccx = I.capCx || 0, ccy = I.capCy || 0;
+  const stemOn = !!(I.stemEnable && I.stemWx > 0 && I.stemWy > 0);
+  const lpts = (cd.loads || []).filter(L => !L._capWeight && !L._stemWeight);
+  const xs = [], ys = [];
+  piles.forEach(p => { xs.push(p.xg - D / 2, p.xg + D / 2); ys.push(p.yg - D / 2, p.yg + D / 2); });
+  if (capOn) { xs.push(ccx - I.capL / 2, ccx + I.capL / 2); ys.push(ccy - I.capW / 2, ccy + I.capW / 2); }
+  if (stemOn) { xs.push((I.stemX || 0) - I.stemWx / 2, (I.stemX || 0) + I.stemWx / 2); ys.push((I.stemY || 0) - I.stemWy / 2, (I.stemY || 0) + I.stemWy / 2); }
```

## 2026-10-10 — PR: claude/pile-o24-o26 (PR link added after merge)

Engineer's decision 2026-10-10 on O24–O26: "Yes go ahead with the others and merge". Basis as stated in `fixlog/README.md`, plus Reese (1997) for weak rock.

### F16. Lateral solve re-runs when the buckling settings change (O26)   [calc behaviour] [no result change for a freshly loaded project]
- **Where:** `App`, the dependency arrays of the `pyRes` memo, the `setCaseRes(null)` effect and the `setPcr(null)` effect (≈ lines 12496, 12572, 12578). Anchor texts: `const pyRes = useMemo(() => {` (array at its closing `}, [I.lateralSource, …`), `React.useEffect(() => { setCaseRes(null); }`, `React.useEffect(() => { setPcr(null); }`.
- **Problem:** `buildPySetup` reads `I.bucklingEnable` and `I.LuFree`: with buckling enabled, the soil springs are removed over the unsupported length below grade. The `pyRes` memo did not list either, so toggling buckling or changing "Added unsupported length" did not re-run the lateral solve. The screen kept the old Mmax, deflection and fixity until some listed input changed, while a reload of the same project gave different numbers. The two explicit-run results that also use `buildPySetup` had the same kind of gap: the case envelope ("Run all cases") was not cleared when the H-pile section, `E`, `solverLembed` or the lateral source changed, and the Pcr ramp was not cleared when buckling, the casing/bond lengths, the bar/grout inputs or φc changed. Either could leave a result for the previous model on screen.
- **Audit:** every input read by `buildPySetup`, by the `pyRes` body and by `solvePyPile`'s arguments was checked against each list. `solvePyPile` only reads its arguments. `pyRes` was missing only `I.bucklingEnable` and `I.LuFree`; the derived EI values it uses (`EI`, `EI_composite_kipin2`, `EI_aashto_kipin2`, `EI_uncased_kipin2`) were already listed. The case envelope deliberately keeps the M-φ curves at the active case's axial load, so `I.STL` stays out of its list (switching the active case must not clear it).
- **Governing provision:** none; no formula, factor or unit changed. This is when the existing calculation runs.
- **Before / After (appended to the end of each array):**
  ```js
  // pyRes memo: before
  … I.pileType, I.hpD, I.hpBf, I.hpTf, I.hpTw, I.hpFy, I.hpAxis, I.solverLembed]);
  // pyRes memo: after
  … I.pileType, I.hpD, I.hpBf, I.hpTf, I.hpTw, I.hpFy, I.hpAxis, I.solverLembed, I.bucklingEnable, I.LuFree]);

  // setCaseRes(null) effect: before
  … I.solverHead, I.solverFree, I.bucklingEnable, I.LuFree, I.Kb, I.pileType]);
  // after
  … I.solverHead, I.solverFree, I.bucklingEnable, I.LuFree, I.Kb, I.pileType, I.lateralSource, I.E, I.solverLembed, I.hpD, I.hpBf, I.hpTf, I.hpTw, I.hpFy, I.hpAxis]);

  // setPcr(null) effect: before
  … I.bklCapMult, I.pyEIvar, I.pyEIBasis, I.pyPM, I.pyYM, JSON.stringify(I.loadCases)]);
  // after
  … I.bklCapMult, I.pyEIvar, I.pyEIBasis, I.pyPM, I.pyYM, JSON.stringify(I.loadCases), I.bucklingEnable, I.Lcased, I.Lplunge, I.LbProvided, I.Ab, I.fyb, I.fcGrout, I.fc, I.phiC, I.hpPhiC]);
  ```
- **Check case:** micropile defaults with the layered profile sand 0 ft (φ 34°, k 110) / soft clay 8 ft (su 600 psf) / stiff clay 16 ft (su 2,500 psf) / sand 25 ft (φ 38°, k 125). Stickup 3 ft, buckling off, then in the UI turn buckling on and set "Added unsupported length" = 8 ft (L_u = 3 + 8 = 11 ft, so 8 ft × 12 = 96 in of springs removed below grade).
  | state | Mmax (kip·ft) | at (ft) | head y (in) | z_fix (ft) | springs removed (in) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | fresh load, buckling off (both) | 51.149 | 3.83 | 2.9767 | 12.92 | 0 |
  | before: after the UI edits | 51.149 | 3.83 | 2.9767 | 12.92 | 0 (stale) |
  | before: reload of the same project | 19.289 | 8.38 | −13.956 | 13.87 | 96 |
  | after: after the UI edits | 19.289 | 8.38 | −13.956 | 13.87 | 96 |
  | after: reload of the same project | 19.289 | 8.38 | −13.956 | 13.87 | 96 |

  Second case, saved with buckling off and L_u = 11 ft, then only the toggle switched on: before, the screen stayed at 51.149 kip·ft while a reload gave 19.289; after, the toggle gives 19.289, equal to the reload.
- **How verified:** headless Chromium, main and branch, the UI sequence above (`o26.mjs`), reading the `pyRes` object from the React state. Fresh loads give identical results on main and branch: page text of every mode identical for the defaults, the four-layer profile, and the four-layer profile with buckling on and 8 ft of added unsupported length (except the H-pile lateral changes from F18).
- **Other copies of this code:** none.

### F17. Weak-rock p-y curves in the solver's units (lb, in) (O24)   [calc change] [LESS conservative than before for deflection and, in the example, for moment; the old springs were 1000× too soft]
- **Where:** `PY.weakrock.pu`, `PY.weakrock.p`, and the weak-rock line of `pySecantEs` (≈ lines 1664, 1673, 1710). Anchor texts: `weakrock: { // Reese (1997) interim weak-rock criterion`, `if (model === 'weakrock') { const b = prm.D;`.
- **Problem:** the lateral solver works in lb and in (`Pt = Plat·1000`, sand γ in lb/in³, clay su in psi), and every p-y curve must return p in lb/in. The weak-rock inputs are labelled and stored in ksi (q_u "ksi", E_m "ksi"; the LPILE importer converts psi → ksi; the AI soil prompt asks for ksi), and `PY.weakrock` used them directly, so p_ur came out in kip/in and K_ir in kip/in², read by the solver as lb/in. Every weak-rock spring was 1000× too soft. That also distorted the Georgiadis layering: a rock layer under soil got an equivalent depth of about 300 ft. Labels, defaults (q_u 1.0 ksi, E_m 300 ksi) and the importer all agree on ksi, so the intent is not ambiguous. The fix converts ksi → psi inside the model, so saved projects keep their ksi values and no stored data changes.
- **Input fields checked (unit label vs use):** q_u: labelled ksi in the layer table, soil-profile drawing, report and AI prompt; LPILE import psi/1000 → ksi; now ×1000 to psi in the model. E_m (Reese's E_ir, initial rock modulus): the same, ksi → psi. RQD (%) → α_r = max(1 − (2/3)·RQD/100, 0.33), unchanged. k_rm: dimensionless (default 0.0005), unchanged. b: in, unchanged. γ is not used by the weak-rock curve.
- **Governing provision:** Reese, L.C. (1997), "Analysis of laterally loaded piles in weak rock", J. Geotech. Geoenviron. Eng. 123(11), 1010–1017 (interim criterion, as also implemented in LPILE):
  - p_ur = α_r·q_ur·b·(1 + 1.4·x_r/b) for 0 ≤ x_r ≤ 3b; p_ur = 5.2·α_r·q_ur·b for x_r ≥ 3b
  - K_ir = k_ir·E_ir, with k_ir = 100 + 400·x_r/(3b) for x_r ≤ 3b and 500 below
  - y_rm = k_rm·b; y_A = [p_ur / (2·y_rm^0.25·K_ir)]^(4/3)
  - p = K_ir·y for y ≤ y_A; p = (p_ur/2)·(y/y_rm)^0.25 for y_A < y < 16·y_rm; p = p_ur beyond.
  The formulas are unchanged; only the units of q_ur and E_ir change.
- **Before:**
  ```js
      const b = prm.D, qu = prm.qu, ar = prm.alpha;   // qu ksi, b in -> pur kip/in
  …
      const Kir = kir * prm.Em;                        // kip/in per in
  …
  ```

### F18. H-pile p-y model: the toe at the embedded length below grade (O25)   [calc change] [at the defaults: no practical change (Mmax −0.005 %); for short embedment: Mmax up (more conservative), head deflection down (LESS conservative)]
- **Where:** `App` → `buildPySetup`, the `bondBottom` H-pile branch (≈ line 12210). Anchor text: `const bondBottom = isHP`.
- **Problem:** the H-pile input is "Embedded length, below grade" (`I.solverLembed`), and stickup is "+ above grade / NEGATIVE = head below grade". Module G's elevation plot and the soil-profile drawing put the toe at `solverLembed` below grade. `buildPySetup` used `solverLembed` as the pile length from the head, so with a 3 ft stickup the p-y pile ended 3 ft short: 27 ft instead of 30 ft below grade. The drawing marked this with a red dashed "p-y model toe" line. The micropile path is correct: it measures its lengths from the head, as its labels say ("Cased length, head → tip"), with soil from grade (`zg = stick_in`), and it is unchanged. Labels are unambiguous: toe = `solverLembed` below grade.
- **Governing provision:** none (model geometry). Basis: the input labels and Module G's geometry.
- **Before:**
  ```js
      // H-pile length: embedment is user cap-embed + solver embed length (no casing/bond concept).
      const bondBottom = isHP
        ? Math.max((I.solverLembed || 30), 5)  // ft from head; reuse solver embed length control
  ```
- **After:**
  ```js
      // H-pile length: "Embedded length, below grade" (I.solverLembed) is measured from GRADE,
      // as Module G and the soil-profile drawing use it: the toe is solverLembed below grade, so
      // the pile length from the head is stickup + solverLembed (stickup signed: + above grade,
      // - head below grade). Before F18 (O25) solverLembed was used as the length from the head.
      const bondBottom = isHP
        ? Math.max(Math.max((I.solverLembed || 30), 5) + (I.solverFree || 0), 5)  // ft from head = stickup + embedded length below grade (>= 5 ft)
  ```
- **Check case 1 (H-pile defaults: HP 13.83×14.70 strong axis, stickup 3 ft, L_embed 30 ft, uniform sand, 6 kip, free head):**
  - Before: L = max(30, 5) = 30 ft = 360 in from the head; embedded = 360 − 36 = 324 in = **27.0 ft** below grade.
  - After: L = max(30, 5) + 3 = 33 ft = 396 in; embedded = 396 − 36 = 360 in = **30.0 ft** below grade, the same as the drawn toe.
  | result | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | modelled toe below grade | 27.0 ft | 30.0 ft |
  | Mmax | 34.884 kip·ft at 4.25 ft | 34.882 kip·ft at 4.43 ft |
  | head deflection | 0.17670 in | 0.17668 in |
  | depth to fixity | 15.76 ft | 15.76 ft |
  | Module 04 flexure D/C | 0.06487 | 0.06486 |
  | Module 05 combined D/C (governing structural) | 0.11243 | 0.11243 |
  | shear / axial D/C | 0.0267 / 0.1110 | 0.0267 / 0.1110 |
  The pile is long and flexible, so the extra 3 ft has no practical effect. The Mmax depth moves by one node because the node spacing is L/120.
- **Check case 2 (the same pile with L_embed = 12 ft):** toe 9.0 → 12.0 ft below grade; Mmax 33.38 → 34.09 kip·ft (+2.1 %, more conservative); head deflection 0.659 → 0.225 in (less conservative); depth to fixity 9.00 → 12.00 ft (the toe in both); flexure D/C 0.0621 → 0.0634.
- **Drawing:** the red dashed "p-y model toe" mark no longer appears, because the p-y toe and the drawn toe now agree. The guard that draws it is kept: it only appears if the 5 ft minimum length overrides the input (embedded length under 5 ft, or a buried head deeper than the embedded length).
- **Also affected:** the case envelope and the Pcr ramp use the same `buildPySetup` length for H-piles.
- **Saved projects affected:** H-pile projects using the built-in p-y analysis with a non-zero stickup. With a stickup of 0 the length is unchanged. With a negative stickup (buried cap) the pile is now shorter: the toe is at `solverLembed` below grade, not `solverLembed` below the head.
- **How verified:** headless Chromium, main vs branch, H-pile defaults and L_embed = 12 ft (`res.mjs`); page text of the micropile and IAB modes identical; the drawing now shows only "toe 30.0 ft".

Engineer's decision 2026-10-10 on O29, O31, O32 (and O33 if trivial): "Go ahead". Basis as stated in `fixlog/README.md` (AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024)). O33 was looked at and left open: see O33 below.

### F19. H-pile static axial capacity: skin from grade (or the buried head) to the toe at the embedded length below grade (O31)   [calc change] [depends on the profile: no change in a uniform profile; MORE conservative or LESS conservative in a layered one — see the check cases]
- **Where:** `computeAll`, the H-pile geotechnical block (≈ line 3449), and `App` → Module G "Geometry summary" table (≈ line 14393). Anchor texts: `// ---- H-PILE geotechnical axial capacity` and `["Pile toe depth",`. `hpileGeoCapacity` itself is unchanged.
- **Problem:** `hpileGeoCapacity` documents `embedTop` as "depth from grade to pile head (0 if at grade)" and `embedLen` as "embedded length below grade", with the toe at `embedTop + embedLen` below grade. `computeAll` passed `embedTop = I.solverFree`, the stickup, which is + ABOVE grade. At the defaults (3 ft stickup, 30 ft embedded) skin friction was counted from 3 to 33 ft below grade and the tip taken at 33 ft, while the input ("Embedded length, below grade"), Module G's elevation, the soil-profile drawing and the p-y model (F18) put the toe at 30 ft with soil from grade. Module G's "Pile toe depth" line printed stickup + embedded length (33.0 ft). With a buried head (negative stickup) the axial interval ran from grade (soil above the head was counted) to `solverLembed` below the head.
- **Code checked for a deliberate reason:** there is no separate "top of skin friction", scour, downdrag or neglected-zone input in the H-pile axial path. `LuFree` (added unsupported length) is used only by buckling and the p-y bracing, not by the axial capacity; the cap embedment (`hpCapEmbed`, inches into the cap) is used only by the head-fixity check. Nothing indicates the 3 ft shift was intended.
- **Governing provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) Art. 10.7.3.8.6 (static analysis): R_n = R_p + R_s, Eq. 10.7.3.8.6a-2/-3/-4; side resistance over the embedded length in contact with soil. Unit values unchanged: sand q_s = N̄60/50 ksf (Eq. 10.7.3.8.6g-3, nondisplacement H-pile), q_p = 0.8·N60·D_b/D ≤ q_L = 8·N60 (sand) / 6·N60 (silt) (Eq. 10.7.3.8.6g-1); clay q_s = α·S_u (Eq. 10.7.3.8.6b-1), q_p = 9·S_u (Eq. 10.7.3.8.6e-1). φ from Table 10.5.5.2.3-1 (inputs `hpPhiGeo`, `hpPhiGeoClay`, `hpPhiUp`), unchanged. Box perimeter and box tip area per C10.7.3.8.6f, unchanged. Only the depth interval changes.
- **Before:**
  ```js
      const embedTop_ft = (I.solverFree || 0);        // depth grade→head (0 at grade)
      const embedLen_ft = Math.max((I.solverLembed || 30), 1);
  …
             ["Pile toe depth", fmt(Math.max(I.solverFree || 0, 0) + Math.max(I.solverLembed || 30, 1), 1) + " ft below grade"],
  ```
- **After:**
  ```js
      // Datum (F19/O31): "Embedded length, below grade" (I.solverLembed) puts the toe at
      // solverLembed below GRADE, as Module G, the soil-profile drawing and the p-y model
      // (F18) do. Stickup I.solverFree is signed (+ above grade, - head below grade), so the
      // soil contact starts at grade, or at the head when the head is buried. Before O31 the
      // stickup was passed as the depth grade->head, so skin ran from stickup to
      // stickup + solverLembed below grade (3-33 ft at the defaults).
      const toe_ft = Math.max((I.solverLembed || 30), 1);                       // grade -> toe (ft)
      const embedTop_ft = Math.min(Math.max(-(I.solverFree || 0), 0), toe_ft);  // depth grade->head when buried, else 0
      const embedLen_ft = toe_ft - embedTop_ft;                                 // soil contact length, head/grade -> toe (ft)
  …
             ["Pile toe depth", fmt(Math.max(I.solverLembed || 30, 1), 1) + " ft below grade"],
  ```
  Interval, before → after: stickup s ≥ 0: [s, s + L] → [0, L]; buried head at depth h (s = −h): [0, L − h] (soil above the head counted, toe short by h) → [h, L]. Toe always at L = `solverLembed` below grade, as in F18 (the p-y model) and the drawing. The 1 ft minimum on L is kept. If a buried head is entered deeper than L, the side length is 0 (it was negative-clipped before as well).

## 2026-10-11 — PR: claude/pile-o33-o34 (PR link added after merge)

Engineer's decision 2026-10-11: "Go ahead with O33 and O34". For O33 the approved behaviour is to keep treating a solve that needs the retry as failed unless the retried solution is a sound, converged equilibrium, and to replace the JavaScript error with a deliberate "did not converge" outcome that makes the lateral-dependent checks NG. Basis as stated in `fixlog/README.md` (AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024)). No AASHTO formula, load or resistance factor, unit or code reference changes in F22 or F23.

### F22. p-y solves that need the adaptive retry: a deliberate "did not converge" outcome instead of a JavaScript error; lateral-dependent checks NG (O33)   [calc behaviour / check status] [MORE conservative for every case found: checks that showed OK on the linear-Winkler fallback moment are now NG. LESS conservative only if a retried solve passes all four acceptance tests (then its moment is used and the stability check passes); no such case was found with the shipped bound]
- **Where:**
  - New top-level code after `solvePyPile` (≈ lines 2211–2276): `PY_NC_MSG`, `PY_NC_TEX`, `PY_LAT_ROW`, `PY_RETRY_CLOSURE_PCT`, `PY_RETRY_DEFL_D`, `pyRetryCheck`, `PyNoConvNote`, `solvePyWithRetry`. Anchor text: `/* F22 (O33) / F23 (O34): the lateral p-y solve used by Module 02`.
  - `App` → `pyRes` memo (≈ line 12709). Anchor text: `const pyRes = useMemo(() => {`.
  - `computeAll`, just before `// ---- overall ----` (≈ line 3880). Anchor text: `// ---- F22 (O33): the lateral p-y solve did not converge ----`.
  - `App` → the live `computeAll(I, {…})` call in the `r` memo (≈ line 13532). Anchor text: `pyStabMsg: (pyRes && !pyRes.ok) ? pyRes.msg : null,`.
  - `App` → `runAllCases` (≈ line 12979), see also F23. Anchor text: `function runAllCases() {`.
  - Displays (listed under "Display changes" below).
- **Problem (from O33):** in `pyRes`, a failed first attempt (8 load steps) triggered an adaptive retry (16 steps, ω 0.55), but the depth records then read `shear: res.V[i]` from the failed first attempt, which has no `V`. Every solve that needed the retry threw, and `pyRes` became `{ ok: false, msg: "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')" }`. The screen and report showed that JavaScript text. The stability check was NG (any p-y failure is), but Module 04 / 05 / 05b, the casing-extension and uncased-flexure checks were evaluated on the **linear-Winkler fallback moment** and could show OK. Fixing only the array name would have switched the retry on for the first time: in every case found, the retry "converges" to a **post-critical** equilibrium (head deflection reversed, 17–170 in) whose equilibrium closure is still excellent (≤ 0.1 % in most), so closure alone cannot tell a sound solution from a post-critical one.
- **Decision implemented:**
  1. The first attempt is unchanged (8 steps, maxIter 200). A solve that converges there is used as before, bit for bit.
  2. Only if it fails: the retry (16 steps, maxIter 400, ω 0.55), unchanged settings.
  3. A retried solution is used only if all four tests pass (`pyRetryCheck`):
     - (a) every load step converged (the solver's own test, `dMax < max(tol, tol·|y0|)`, tol = 1e-6);
     - (b) equilibrium closure ΣF ≤ 1 % and ΣM ≤ 1 % (`res.eq`, the residuals the tool already reports);
     - (c) stable loading branch: the head deflection keeps the sign of the first load step and |y0| never drops by more than 0.1 % from its running peak (the same fold-back rule the pushover plot already uses);
     - (d) sanity bound: |y0| ≤ 1.0 × D, D = the p-y pile width in the bending plane (casing OD for a micropile; the H-pile width the p-y curves use).
  4. Otherwise (retry fails, or any test fails): `pyRes = { ok: false, noConv: true, msg: PY_NC_MSG, why: [...] }`, shown as **"Did not converge — the pile is likely unstable (buckling / P-Δ) at this load"** with the reason and what to do. `computeAll` gets `pyNoConv` and sets `R.lateralNoConv`; flexure, combined loading, CFST P-M, casing extension, uncased flexure (micropile) and H-pile flexure / combined become NG; combined-loading stability was already NG and stays NG. The P-y-independent checks (geotechnical, axial, shear, bearing, punching, tension, buckling by the selected method) are unchanged.
  5. The criteria are written into the Methodology text (DocsModal "02 · Lateral analysis", new paragraph "Nonlinear p-y convergence").
- **Governing provision:** none changed. The acceptance tests are numerical-solution criteria chosen by the tool, not code provisions: closure 1 % and the one-pile-width bound are judgement values (see O37). The stability row keeps its existing reference "AASHTO 6.9.4 / p-y".

- **New code after `solvePyPile` (after only; nothing before):**
  ```js
  const PY_NC_MSG = "Did not converge — the pile is likely unstable (buckling / P-Δ) at this load";
  // shown (KaTeX) in place of a check comparison that needs the lateral solution
  const PY_NC_TEX = "\\text{NG: the lateral p-y solve did not converge (no valid moment demand)}";
  // summary-table / dashboard rows whose demand comes from the lateral solution
  const PY_LAT_ROW = /^(Flexure|Combined axial \+ flexure|Combined \(interaction\)|Casing flexure|Combined loading \(casing-only|Combined \(casing\)|Combined loading \(CFST P-M\)|Combined \(CFST P-M\)|Casing past active moment zone|Uncased flexure)/;
  const PY_RETRY_CLOSURE_PCT = 1.0;   // max equilibrium residual (% of applied) for a retried solve
  const PY_RETRY_DEFL_D = 1.0;        // max |head deflection| for a retried solve, in pile widths D
  function pyRetryCheck(rr, D) {
    const why = [];
    const eq = rr.eq || {};
    if (!(eq.fPct <= PY_RETRY_CLOSURE_PCT && eq.mPct <= PY_RETRY_CLOSURE_PCT))
      why.push("equilibrium closure ΣF " + fmt(eq.fPct, 2) + " % / ΣM " + fmt(eq.mPct, 2) + " % exceeds " + fmt(PY_RETRY_CLOSURE_PCT, 1) + " %");
    // Stable loading branch: the head deflection keeps the direction of the first load step
    // and |y0| never drops while the load rises (same fold-back rule as the pushover plot).
    const h = rr.history || [];
    const y1 = h.length ? h[0].y0 : 0;
    let peak = 0, flip = false, fold = false;
    for (const s of h) {
      if (Math.abs(y1) > 1e-9 && s.y0 * y1 < 0) flip = true;
      const mag = Math.abs(s.y0);
      if (mag < peak * (1 - 1e-3)) fold = true;
      peak = Math.max(peak, mag);
    }
    if (flip) why.push("the head deflection reversed direction during the load ramp (post-critical equilibrium)");
    else if (fold) why.push("the head deflection decreased while the load increased (fold-back, post-critical equilibrium)");
    const y0 = rr.y && rr.y.length ? rr.y[0] : NaN;
    if (!(Math.abs(y0) <= PY_RETRY_DEFL_D * D))
      why.push("head deflection " + fmt(Math.abs(y0), 2) + " in exceeds the sanity bound of " + (PY_RETRY_DEFL_D === 1 ? "one pile width" : fmt(PY_RETRY_DEFL_D, 1) + " pile widths") + " (" + fmt(PY_RETRY_DEFL_D * D, 2) + " in)");
    return why;
  }
  function PyNoConvNote({ why, print }) { … }   // the message, "Reason: …" and "What to do: …" (screen and print)
  function solvePyWithRetry(input, D) {
    const res = solvePyPile({ ...input, nSteps: 8, maxIter: 200 });
    if (res.ok) return { res, retried: false, noConv: false, why: [] };
    const res2 = solvePyPile({ ...input, nSteps: 16, maxIter: 400, omega: 0.55 });
    if (!res2.ok) {
      const last = res2.history.length ? res2.history[res2.history.length - 1] : null;
      return { res: null, retried: true, noConv: true,
        why: ["the first solve (8 load steps) and the adaptive retry (16 load steps, under-relaxed) both failed to converge" + (last ? "; the retry stopped at load step " + last.step + "/16 (lateral " + fmt(last.P / 1000, 2) + " kip, axial " + fmt(last.Q / 1000, 1) + " kip)" : "")] };
    }
    const why = pyRetryCheck(res2, D);
    if (why.length) return { res: null, retried: true, noConv: true, why: ["the first solve (8 load steps) did not converge; the adaptive retry (16 load steps) was rejected: " + why.join("; ")] };
    return { res: res2, retried: true, noConv: false, why: [] };
  }
  ```
  (`PyNoConvNote` text: "✗ NG — <PY_NC_MSG>. The built-in p-y solve found no converged, stable equilibrium at the design loads, so there is no valid lateral demand: the checks that use the lateral moment (flexure, combined loading and, for a micropile, casing extension and uncased flexure) are NG, and so is combined-loading stability." + "Reason: …" + "What to do: reduce the axial and/or lateral load; check buckling and P_cr in Module 10 (the nonlinear P-crit ramp shows the thrust at which the pile becomes unstable); shorten the unsupported length (stickup, scour, added unsupported length); or add stiffness (larger section, longer casing).")

- **Date:** 2026-10-11. **Type:** UI only. Review of the F24 screenshots, the same day (display only, no calc change).
- **What changed:**
  - **One datum: depth below grade** (stickup negative), axis title "depth below grade (ft)", a dashed grade line at 0 (`latGradeLine`), hover "depth … ft below grade", on every lateral graph:
    - Figure F-1 (`LpileProfilePlot`) on screen **and in the printed report**: new optional `zOffset` (ft). With it the records' depth from the pile head is drawn less the stickup: `pyRes.setup.stick_in / 12` (the solver's datum, the one Figure F-3, F-2 and the report table use). The three panels now share one depth axis (`matches: "y"`), so grade lines up across them (before, each panel autoranged on its own). Without `zOffset` the plot is as before (no other caller).
    - F-1 single views (`LatProfileOne`), Soil reaction, Soil mobilization (now also drawn over the soil-reaction chart's depth range, pile head to toe), EI along the pile (depths from the solver nodes, so the stickup is no longer folded onto grade; `eiProf.d` itself is unchanged), F-2 on screen; F-2 in the report gets the grade line (it was already below grade).
    - `LateralDiagram` (linear basis and the built-in vs LPILE comparison): title "depth z (ft)" → "depth below grade (ft)"; the two panels share one depth axis; **the LPILE overlay is shifted by the project stickup** (LPILE reports depth from its pile head; before, it was drawn as if that were depth below grade, i.e. the LPILE head at grade). The unnamed helper traces no longer appear in the legend ("trace 1", "trace 2"); the legend has a fixed entry width; the "P=…k" label is no longer clipped.
    - LPILE comparison profiles: drawn below grade with this project's stickup; the note says so and that this holds when the LPILE model has the same stickup.
    - Figure F-3 has no depth axis; its depth chips and table were already in ft below grade (unchanged).
  - **Elevation moment diagram** (`ElevationPlot`): fixed depth range from the pile head (less 16 % of the span, at least 2 ft, for the load arrows and label) to the toe + 3 ft (before: autorange about −45 to +40 ft, because the axial-load label was placed with an invalid `yref: "pixel"` and read as data y = −46). Loads: the P and V arrows are kept; one label "P = … kip · V = … kip (· ↻ M = …)" sits above the head, right of the axial arrow (before, "V = …" overlapped the head arrow and the cap). The "Mmax …" label is drawn outside the plot area if needed (`cliponaxis: false`, right margin 64 px) instead of being clipped.
  - **Summary tab**: the small "Moment profiles · all cases overlaid" chart in the case-envelope card is replaced by a link "Moment profiles of all cases (Figure F-2) are on the Lateral graphs tab: Moment — all cases →". It was screen only (the printed report has its own F-2), so nothing is kept for print.
- **Not changed:** every computed value and every number in the report text; the plotted x values; F-3 data.
- **Check (datum):** report F-1, origin/main vs branch, micropile defaults: every x value identical, every y value lower by exactly 3.000000000 ft = the stickup; y title "depth (ft)" → "depth below grade (ft)".
- **How verified:** `node --check`; the parity run of F24 repeated (report text, output text outside Module 02, statuses, saved data, export, IndexedDB, hand-off identical); F-3 cross-check on the Plotly data repeated (2.3·10⁻¹⁶ static, 3.3·10⁻¹⁶ cyclic); screenshots of every sub-tab at 1500 and 400 px with the p-y, linear and Input Mmax bases, with an LPILE import and with a solve that does not converge, looked at; Summary link selects Lateral graphs → Moment — all cases; Letter PDF page with F-1 looked at; no console errors; no horizontal scroll at 400 px.
- **Re-applying by hand:** the unified diff below is against the F24 state of the file (CRLF stripped). Anchors: `function LateralDiagram({` (`ovZ`, the four hover texts, `"depth z (ft)"`, the legend, `yaxis2`, the helper traces after `dash: "dot"`), `function LpileProfilePlot({` (`zOffset`, `zLbl`, the three hover texts, the y title, `yaxis2`/`yaxis3`), the report F-1 call `React.createElement(LpileProfilePlot, { records: pyRes.records`, the report F-2 `layout: baseLayout({ height: 240,`, `function ElevationPlot(` (`// ---- Applied loads at the pile head`), `LoadCasesCard` (anchor `"Moment profiles · all cases overlaid"`), and in the Lateral graphs block `latGradeLine`, `LatProfileOne`, the F-1 note, F-2, Soil reaction, Soil mobilization, EI along the pile and the LPILE note.

## 2026-10-11 — PR: claude/pile-o37 (PR link added after merge)

Engineer's decision 2026-10-11 on O37: "The deflection limit will be much smaller than 1D, I don't know what it is, but probably a couple inches. I suggest just leaving it off or maybe an input for the warning with default at .25D." Implemented: the deflection bound is removed from the acceptance of a retried p-y solve, and a new warning input (default 0.25 D) flags a large head deflection everywhere the lateral result is shown. Basis as stated in `fixlog/README.md` (AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024)). No AASHTO formula, load or resistance factor, unit or code reference changes.

### F25. Retried p-y solves: no |y₀| ≤ 1·D acceptance bound; new "Large head-deflection warning" input (default 0.25 D, warning only) (O37)   [calc behaviour / check status] [LESS conservative for acceptance: a retried solve that converges on the stable branch with closure ≤ 1 % but |y₀| > D is now USED (its moment drives the checks and the stability check passes) instead of "did not converge" / NG. The warning itself changes no result]
- **Date:** 2026-10-11. **Type:** calc behaviour (acceptance of a numerical solution) + display (warning).
- **Where:**
  - Top-level, after `solvePyPile`: `pyRetryCheck` (anchor `function pyRetryCheck(rr, D) {`), the constant above it (anchor `const PY_RETRY_CLOSURE_PCT = 1.0;`), the block comment above `PY_NC_MSG` (anchor `3. A retried solution is used only if it passes pyRetryCheck`), and new helpers after `pyRetryCheck` (anchor `/* F25 (O37): large head-deflection WARNING`): `PY_DEFL_WARN_D_DEFAULT`, `pyDeflWarnFactor`, `pyDeflWarnInfo`, `pyDeflWarnText`, `PY_DEFL_WARN_NOTE`.
  - `DEFAULT_INPUTS`: new field `pyDeflWarnD: 0.25` (anchor `pyNodes: 120,`).
  - Input: `App`, rail "Head condition" block (Bond / p-y tab for a micropile, p-y / lateral tab for an H-pile; not shown in integral abutment mode), after `CyclicInfoModal` (anchor `onRevert: () => { set('pyCyclic', false); setCycInfoOpen(false); } })`).
  - Displays: `PyPanel` (Module 02, anchor `// F25 (O37): large head-deflection warning (amber, warning only)` before `"head deflection ", fmt(pyRes.headDefl_in, 3)`); `UtilizationDashboard` (anchor `function UtilizationDashboard({ r, I, pyRes })` and its call `React.createElement(UtilizationDashboard, { r: r, I: I, pyRes: pyRes })`); `LatGraphsCard` (anchor `const dw = ok ? pyDeflWarnInfo(`), `LpileProfilePlot` (new prop `deflWarn`), `LatProfileOne` (new prop `deflWarn`), helper `pyDeflWarnLines` (anchor `function pyDeflWarnLines(w, ys) {`); `LoadCasesCard` envelope (anchor `" ⚠ large defl."`); `runAllCases` row field `D` (anchor `D: S ? S.D : null`); `PrintReport`: solver-settings row (anchor `["Large head-deflection warning",`), 02R row + box (anchors `["Large-deflection warning limit",` and `// F25 (O37): large head-deflection warning (amber, warning only)`), envelope (anchor `" ⚠ large deflection"`); DocsModal "02 · Lateral analysis" text (anchor `Large head deflection: when |y₀| exceeds the factor`).
- **Governing provision:** none. Both the old 1·D bound and the new 0.25·D warning are judgement values chosen for the tool (no AASHTO provision); the service deflection limit (`deflLimit`, "svc defl limit", default 1.00 in) is unchanged and still checked on service rows.
- **Acceptance rule, before → after (retried solves only; a first attempt that converges is used as before, unchanged):**
  | test | before (F22) | after (F25) |
  |---|---|---|
  | (a) every load step converged | required | required |
  | (b) closure ΣF ≤ 1 % and ΣM ≤ 1 % | required | required |
  | (c) stable branch (no sign reversal, no fold-back > 0.1 %) | required | required |
  | (d) \|y₀\| ≤ 1.0 × D | required | **removed** (replaced by the warning below, which does not reject anything) |
- **Before (`pyRetryCheck` and the constant):**
  ```js
  const PY_RETRY_CLOSURE_PCT = 1.0;   // max equilibrium residual (% of applied) for a retried solve
  const PY_RETRY_DEFL_D = 1.0;        // max |head deflection| for a retried solve, in pile widths D
  function pyRetryCheck(rr, D) {
  …
    if (flip) why.push("the head deflection reversed direction during the load ramp (post-critical equilibrium)");
    else if (fold) why.push("the head deflection decreased while the load increased (fold-back, post-critical equilibrium)");
    const y0 = rr.y && rr.y.length ? rr.y[0] : NaN;
    if (!(Math.abs(y0) <= PY_RETRY_DEFL_D * D))
      why.push("head deflection " + fmt(Math.abs(y0), 2) + " in exceeds the sanity bound of " + (PY_RETRY_DEFL_D === 1 ? "one pile width" : fmt(PY_RETRY_DEFL_D, 1) + " pile widths") + " (" + fmt(PY_RETRY_DEFL_D * D, 2) + " in)");
    return why;
  }
  ```
- **After:**
  ```js
  const PY_RETRY_CLOSURE_PCT = 1.0;   // max equilibrium residual (% of applied) for a retried solve
  // F25 (O37): no deflection bound in the acceptance (was PY_RETRY_DEFL_D = 1.0, |y0| <= 1.0 D);
  // a large head deflection is now a warning only (pyDeflWarnInfo).
  function pyRetryCheck(rr, D) {
  …
    if (flip) why.push("the head deflection reversed direction during the load ramp (post-critical equilibrium)");
    else if (fold) why.push("the head deflection decreased while the load increased (fold-back, post-critical equilibrium)");
    return why;
  }
  /* F25 (O37): large head-deflection WARNING (amber; not a check, nothing becomes NG). … */
  const PY_DEFL_WARN_D_DEFAULT = 0.25;
  function pyDeflWarnFactor(I) {
    const v = I ? I.pyDeflWarnD : undefined;
    return (typeof v === "number" && isFinite(v)) ? v : PY_DEFL_WARN_D_DEFAULT;
  }
  // returns null when off / no result, else { f, D, lim, y0, yD, warn }
  function pyDeflWarnInfo(y0, D, I) {
    const f = pyDeflWarnFactor(I);
    if (!(f > 0) || !(D > 0) || y0 == null || !isFinite(y0)) return null;
    const lim = f * D;
    return { f, D, lim, y0, yD: Math.abs(y0) / D, warn: Math.abs(y0) > lim };
  }
  function pyDeflWarnText(w) {
    return "Large head deflection: |y₀| = " + fmt(Math.abs(w.y0), 2) + " in = " + fmt(w.yD, 2) + " D > " + fmt(w.f, 2) + " × D = " + fmt(w.lim, 2) + " in (D = " + fmt(w.D, 2) + " in)";
  }
  const PY_DEFL_WARN_NOTE = "Warning only, not a code check: the lateral checks use this solution as computed. Check the deflection against the structure's tolerance (the service limit is checked separately), and treat a deflection this large, especially one opposite to the applied load, as a sign the pile may be near or past instability (see Module 10).";
  ```
  The block comment above `PY_NC_MSG` now reads "(every step converged, equilibrium closure, stable loading branch; F25 (O37) removed the former |y0| <= 1.0 D bound, see pyDeflWarnInfo …)". Module 02's retried-solve note "closure, stable-branch and deflection checks passed" → "convergence, closure and stable-branch checks passed". The Methodology paragraph "Nonlinear p-y convergence" drops "(d) the head deflection is no more than one pile width D" and "branch and deflection tests" → "branch test", and gains a sentence describing the warning.
- **New input and saved data:**
  - Field `pyDeflWarnD` in the project inputs (the same object as every other input: autosave key `micropile_lrfd_inputs_v1`, Save .json `inputs`, IndexedDB library). Default 0.25 in `DEFAULT_INPUTS`. No key or format change: an older project has no `pyDeflWarnD`, `mergeSavedInputs` fills the default (0.25), and `pyDeflWarnFactor` also falls back to 0.25 if it is ever missing. A blank field is saved as null and restored to 0.25 on reload (with the usual "Blank field(s) … restored" note); 0 or a negative value turns the warning off.
  - UI (rail, under "p-y loading criterion"): heading "Large head-deflection warning", `y₀ > [0.25] × D · 0 = off · blank = 0.25`, and the note "Amber warning, not a check: … The service deflection limit (Loads & group tab) is separate."
  - Main (before this PR) opening a file saved by the branch: the extra field is carried and ignored; results identical (checked, see below).
- **Where the warning shows** (amber, `#b7791f` / `#7a4d15`; never red, never NG; module status chips unchanged). D = the p-y pile width the solve uses (`pyRes.setup.D`, casing OD for a micropile, the H-pile bearing width; per envelope row `S.D`):
  - Module 02: an amber box under the "Governing result" banner: "⚠ WARNING — Large head deflection: |y₀| = … in = … D > 0.25 × D = … in (D = … in). Warning only, not a code check: …".
  - Lateral graphs tab, Figure F-1: dotted amber lines at ±f·D on the deflection panel (all-three view, label "±0.25D = ±1.75 in (warning)") and in the single Deflection view (vertical label "±0.25 × D = ±1.75 in (large-deflection warning)"; both labels on a white backing). The axes are NOT widened (review change requested before merge): a line is drawn only when it falls inside the natural range of the deflection data, [min(y, 0), max(y, 0)] (`pyDeflWarnLines`); when the warning is triggered the line on the side of y₀ is always inside. Under the figure: the amber warning when exceeded; a grey note naming the lines when a line is drawn but not exceeded; otherwise "Large head-deflection warning limit = 3.68 in (0.25 D, D = 14.70 in; …) — not reached: head deflection 0.177 in = 0.01 D. (Outside the plotted range, so no line is drawn.)". Plot ranges are identical to main in every case run (H-pile defaults ±0.203 in, micropile defaults ±3.64 in, cases (i) ±10.81 in and (iii) ±189.4 in).
  - Summary of checks (dashboard): an amber line under the header (button to Module 02): "⚠ Warning — Large head deflection: … Warning only, not a check (no D/C row)."
  - Case envelope (screen): "⚠ large defl." after y₀ in each flagged row, plus a note listing the flagged cases in D. Printed envelope: "⚠ large deflection" after y₀ and the same note.
  - Report: solver-settings row "Large head-deflection warning |y₀| > 0.25 × D"; 02R "Governing result" row "Large-deflection warning limit 1.75 in · 0.25 × D (D = 7.00 in) · EXCEEDED — warning / not exceeded"; when exceeded, an amber box under that table with the warning text.
  - It applies to **every** lateral p-y result (a first attempt and an accepted retry, Module 02 and each envelope case), so it also flags the O36 post-critical first attempts (large, reversed head deflection) that F22 still accepts.
- **Check case (i) — micropile defaults, free head, one strength case STL 20 kip / P 14 kip** (F22 check case 2; 7 in casing, stickup 3 ft, M-φ EI on; D = 7.00 in). First attempt fails at step 8 (> 200 iterations). Retry (16 steps, ω 0.55): every step converges, y₀ rises monotonically to +9.397 in; closure ΣF 0.00028 %, ΣM 0.00004 %; 790 iterations.
  | result | before (main) | after (branch) |
  |---|---|---|
  | acceptance | (a) (b) (c) pass, (d) 9.40 in > 1.0 × 7.00 in **fails** → "did not converge" | (a) (b) (c) pass → **accepted** |
  | Module 02 | ✗ NG — Did not converge (reason: head deflection 9.40 in exceeds the sanity bound of one pile width (7.00 in)) | ✓ Converged · Mmax = 107.84 kip·ft @ 5.1 ft below grade (adaptive retry) + amber warning "|y₀| = 9.40 in = 1.34 D > 0.25 × D = 1.75 in" |
  | Casing flexure (Module 04) | NG (no valid demand) | NG, D/C = 107.84 / 53.95 = **1.999** |
  | Combined (casing) (Module 05) | NG | NG, interaction **2.038** |
  | Combined-loading stability | NG | **OK** (stable) |
  | Uncased flexure (Module G) | NG | **0.44 OK** |
  | Casing past active moment zone | NG | OK (5 % decay at 11.3 ft < casing 12.0 ft) |
  | `allPass` | false | false |

### F26, part b. Lateral graphs show their key values: max / min with depths, capacity and service-limit lines, depth to fixity, key-values strips (screen and report)   [UI only] [no calculation change]
- **Date:** 2026-10-11. **Type:** UI only. Engineer's additions the same day: "Also the graphs should show more info, maybe max/mins, maybe some other detail too?" and "Maybe we add a depth to fixity indicator on the graphs as well."
- **Rule:** every number shown is a value the tool already computes (`pyRes`, `r`, the inputs) or a simple extraction from the solver's own arrays (largest / smallest value and its depth; sign changes located by linear interpolation between solver nodes, as `momentZeroCrossings` does). No new engineering quantity. New helpers (before the elevation block): `latZeros`, `latKV(I, r, pyRes, actType)` (collects the values), `latStack` (label stacking), `latOverlay(K, q, xa, ya, R, o)` (markers, labels, lines for one response panel), `LatKeys` (key-values strip: chips on screen, a two-pair-per-row table in print), `latKeysF1`, `latKeysFix`, `latCaseKeys`.
- **Depth to fixity — the depths the tool already has (no new definition):**
  | Line | Value | Definition / source | Style |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | z_fix (primary, labelled) | `pyRes.zFix2` | 2nd zero crossing of the moment below grade (Module 02 "Geotechnical depth to fixity", reference only) | purple solid |
  | 5 % moment decay | `pyRes.zMomentDecay` | first depth below M_max where \|M\| ≤ 5 % of M_max (Module 02; micropile casing-extension check) | green dash |
  | buckling fixity (only when Module 10 is enabled and its method gives L_f) | `r.buckling.Le_buck − stickup` | equivalent fixed base at head + L_u + L_f (Module 10, method named: Davisson / deflection-matched) | brown dot |
  When there is no 2nd zero crossing the strip says "none — the moment does not reverse below M_max (Module 02)" and the 5 % decay line is the labelled one. Hidden when the solve did not converge (the graphs are not drawn then). H-pile: the same `pyRes` values (the H-pile p-y path computes zFix2 / decay; Module 10 is section-aware).
  Shown on all F-1 panels (screen, single views, report), the elevation (both panels), the soil-reaction chart; in the legend and hover with the full definition; the primary one labelled on the plot; listed in every key strip.
- **Figure F-1** (`LpileProfilePlot` new optional `kv`, `narrow`; `LatProfileOne` new optional `kv`, `narrow`; used only for the built-in p-y solve, not for LPILE imports):
  - Deflection: y₀ (`pyRes.headDefl_in`) labelled; max / min with depth; first zero crossing; toe deflection. Head rotation: the solver does not return it, so it is not shown. **Service deflection limit** `I.deflLimit` (`|| 1`, as the case envelope) as dash-dot lines, **each of ±limit only where it lies inside the deflection range [min(0, y), max(0, y)] (never widens the axis; the same rule as the F25 warning lines, `pyDeflWarnLines`)**, otherwise a note "…not reached (outside the plotted range)"; when the active case is a service case, a tag "service case: |y₀| … ≤/> limit — OK/NG" (same test as `runAllCases`: `|y0| ≤ deflLimit`).
  - Moment: +M max and −M min with depths (labelled), zero-moment depths (`pyRes.mzCrossings`, markers with hover), capacity lines ±φM_n: micropile `r.flex.phiMn` (cased, head to casing tip, Module 04) and `r.geoChecks.phiMn_uncased` (casing tip to toe, Module G); H-pile `r.hpileStruct.phiMn` (Module 04). A capacity line widens the axis only up to 4 × the response; beyond that it is noted "off scale" and listed in the strip. Casing tip line (micropile).
  - Shear: +V max / −V min with depths; H-pile ±φV_n (`r.hpileStruct.phiVn`, Module 07). Micropile: no shear capacity line (the tool has no pile shear capacity; punching is a cap check).
  - Labels stacked ≥ 12 px apart inside the plot; on a narrow card (< 700 px) only the primary labels, shortened; every point keeps a hover. Legend below the plot. Height 520 → 600 px (single views 560 → 640).
- **Elevation (F26 part a):** dimension lines left of the pile — micropile L_cased, L_bond, total length; H-pile embedded length, total length (not on a narrow card; in the hover and strip); fixity lines across both panels; strip "Dimensions and depth to fixity" (scale ×N, stickup, the dimensions with their depth ranges, plunge, OD / d_h / bar or H-pile width, cap embedment, fixity).
- **Figure F-2:** legend "case · Mmax … @ … ft" (`row.Mmax`, depth of the profile node with the largest |M|), governing case (largest Mmax) drawn thicker and "(governs)", envelope max marker; strip with each case and the cases with no profile (did not converge).
- **Figure F-3:** legend adds "p_u … lb/in · p/p_u …" per curve (`pyCurveSet` `pu`, `ratio`, the values of the table under it).
- **Soil reaction:** max |p| with depth (marker + label), layer boundaries (dotted, hover), fixity lines and legend; mobilisation chart: peak p/p_u with depth; strip.
- **Pushover & stiffness:** pushover design point (P = `I.Plat`, y₀ = `pyRes.headDefl_in`); M-φ charts: φM_n cased / uncased lines; EI profile: casing tip line; strip (design point, |M|max, M_cr, φM_n, casing tip; "First yield M_y: not computed by the tool").
- **Printed report:** F-1 drawn with the same markers / lines / legend (440 px tall) followed by "Figure F-1 key values (active case)"; F-2 followed by "Figure F-2 key values (Mmax per case)" when cases were run; F-4 (elevation) followed by "Dimensions and depth to fixity". Not in integral abutment mode (its F-1 prints as before).
- **App:** `LatGraphsCard` gets `r` and `actType` (type of the active case, `cases[activeIdx].type`); both `PrintReport` `gfx` objects get `actType`. CSS `.pd-lg-keys*` added.
- **Not changed:** every computed value, check, report number and saved data. Report text: only additions (the strips and the F-3 legend are new text).
- **Governing provision:** none (presentation only).
- **Check (every annotated number equals the tool's value; automated, headless Chromium):** micropile defaults, micropile d_h 10 in, H-pile defaults, H-pile P = 45 kip, micropile and H-pile with a 4-layer profile and Module 10 enabled, micropile with a service case active:
  - |M|max strip = Module 02 "M_max = … @ … ft" (e.g. 53.4 kip·ft @ 4.1 ft; H-pile 34.9 @ 4.4; layered 25.5 @ 3.2);
  - y₀ strip = Module 02 "head deflection …" (3.162 in; H-pile 0.177 in);
  - z_fix line (F-1, elevation) and strip = Module 02 z_fix (10.7 / 15.8 / 11.3 / 14.4 ft); 5 % decay line and strip = Module 02 (10.0 / 14.6 / 10.3 / 13.8 ft);
  - φM_n cased line = Module 04 φ_f M_n (53.9 kip·ft); φM_n uncased line = Module G φM_n,uncased (0.95 kip·ft); H-pile φM_n = Module 04 (537.8, off scale at the defaults, drawn at P = 45 kip where |M| = 365.8); H-pile φV_n = Module 07 (224.7 kip);
  - casing tip line = 12.0 ft (Lcased 15 − stickup 3); no casing tip line in H-pile mode;
  - service limit = the input (1.00 in); service case active (Svc I, P = 4 kip): |y₀| 1.354 > 1.00 → "NG", the same test as the case envelope;
  - buckling fixity uses Module 10's L_u + L_f (e.g. 3.0 + 4.8 = 7.8 ft from the head → 4.8 ft below grade, Davisson).

```diff
+/* ---- F26 part b: key values on the lateral graphs (display only) ----
+   Engineer 2026-10-11: "the graphs should show more info, maybe max/mins" and
+   "maybe we add a depth to fixity indicator on the graphs as well". Every
+   number is read from pyRes / r / the inputs, or is a simple extraction from
+   the solver's own arrays (max / min and their depth; sign changes found by
+   linear interpolation between solver nodes). No new engineering quantity. */
+function latZeros(z, v) {
+  const out = [];
+  for (let i = 1; i < v.length; i++) {
+    const a = v[i - 1], b = v[i];
+    if ((a < 0 && b > 0) || (a > 0 && b < 0)) out.push(z[i - 1] + (z[i] - z[i - 1]) * a / (a - b));
+  }
+  return out;
+}
+function latKV(I, r, pyRes, actType) {
+  if (!pyRes || !pyRes.ok || !pyRes.records || pyRes.records.length < 3) return null;
+  const s = pyRes.setup ? pyRes.setup.stick_in / 12 : (I.solverFree || 0);
+  const rec = pyRes.records, n = rec.length;
+  const z = rec.map(q => q.depth - s), y = rec.map(q => q.defl), M = rec.map(q => q.mom), V = rec.map(q => q.shear);
+  const at = (a, i) => ({ v: a[i], z: z[i], i });
+  const iMax = a => a.reduce((k, v, i) => v > a[k] ? i : k, 0), iMin = a => a.reduce((k, v, i) => v < a[k] ? i : k, 0);
+  const isHP = I.pileType === "hpile";
+  const K = { s, z, y, M, V, isHP, zTop: z[0], zBot: z[n - 1] };
+  K.y0 = pyRes.headDefl_in; K.yToe = y[n - 1];
+  K.yMax = at(y, iMax(y)); K.yMin = at(y, iMin(y));
+  const yz = latZeros(z, y); K.yZero = yz.length ? yz[0] : null;
+  const lim = I.deflLimit || 1;   // as the case envelope's service check (runAllCases)
+  K.svc = { lim, active: actType === "service", ok: Math.abs(K.y0) <= lim };
+  K.Mpos = at(M, iMax(M)); K.Mneg = at(M, iMin(M));
+  K.Mmax = pyRes.Mmax_kft; K.zMmax = pyRes.zMmax;
+  K.Mzeros = Array.isArray(pyRes.mzCrossings) ? pyRes.mzCrossings.slice() : [];
+  K.Vpos = at(V, iMax(V)); K.Vneg = at(V, iMin(V));
+  K.cap = []; K.Vcap = null; K.tip = null;
+  if (isHP) {
+    if (r && r.hpileStruct) {
+      K.cap.push({ v: r.hpileStruct.phiMn, z0: K.zTop, z1: K.zBot, lbl: "φM_n (Module 04)", short: "φMn" });
+      K.Vcap = { v: r.hpileStruct.phiVn, lbl: "φV_n (Module 07)" };
+    }
+  } else if (r && r.flex && r.geo) {
+    K.tip = r.geo.casingTip - s;
+    K.Mtip = pyRes.Mtip_kft;
+    K.cap.push({ v: r.flex.phiMn, z0: K.zTop, z1: Math.min(K.tip, K.zBot), lbl: "φM_n cased (Module 04)", short: "φMn cased" });
+    if (r.geoChecks && K.tip < K.zBot) K.cap.push({ v: r.geoChecks.phiMn_uncased, z0: K.tip, z1: K.zBot, lbl: "φM_n uncased (Module G)", short: "φMn uncased", dp: 2 });
+  }
+  // depth to fixity: the depths the tool already computes, each with its definition and source
+  K.fix = [];
+  if (pyRes.zFix2 != null && isFinite(pyRes.zFix2)) K.fix.push({ k: "zfix", z: pyRes.zFix2, col: "#7a4a7a", dash: "solid",
+    name: "z_fix " + fmt(pyRes.zFix2, 1) + " ft (2nd M zero)",
+    lbl: "z_fix = " + fmt(pyRes.zFix2, 1) + " ft — 2nd zero crossing of moment (Module 02, reference)" });
+  if (pyRes.zMomentDecay != null && isFinite(pyRes.zMomentDecay)) K.fix.push({ k: "decay", z: pyRes.zMomentDecay, col: "#2f6f3e", dash: "dash",
+    name: "5% M decay " + fmt(pyRes.zMomentDecay, 1) + " ft",
+    lbl: "5% moment-decay depth = " + fmt(pyRes.zMomentDecay, 1) + " ft — first depth below M_max where |M| ≤ 5% of M_max (Module 02" + (isHP ? ")" : "; casing-extension check)") });
+  const b = r && r.buckling;
+  if (b && b.enable && b.Lf_buck != null && isFinite(b.Lf_buck) && isFinite(b.Le_buck)) K.fix.push({ k: "bkl", z: b.Le_buck - s, col: "#8a5a1f", dash: "dot",
+    name: "buckling fixity " + fmt(b.Le_buck - s, 1) + " ft (Module 10)",
+    lbl: "buckling equivalent fixed base = head + L_u + L_f = " + fmt(b.Lu_free, 1) + " + " + fmt(b.Lf_buck, 1) + " = " + fmt(b.Le_buck, 1) + " ft below the head, " + fmt(b.Le_buck - s, 1) + " ft below grade (Module 10, " + (b.lfGoverning && b.lfGoverning.src ? b.lfGoverning.src : (b.bklTab || "")) + ")" });
+  K.fix.forEach((f, i) => { f.primary = i === 0; });
+  return K;
+}
+/* stack labels on one side of a panel: depth y (ft) wanted, at least `gap` ft apart, inside [lo, hi] */
+function latStack(list, gap, lo, hi) {
+  list.sort((a, b) => a.y - b.y);
+  let cur = -Infinity;
+  list.forEach(L => { L.ly = Math.max(L.y, cur + gap, lo); cur = L.ly; });
+  let lim = hi;
+  for (let k = list.length - 1; k >= 0; k--) { if (list[k].ly > lim) list[k].ly = lim; lim = list[k].ly - gap; }
+  return list;
+}
+/* markers, labels, capacity / limit lines and fixity lines for one response
+   panel (q = "y" | "M" | "V") on axes xa / ya; R = the panel's x range.
+   o: { narrow, legend (show legend entries), pxFt, zLo, zHi, fixLabel } */
+function latOverlay(K, q, xa, ya, R, o) {
```

### F26, part b — review polish (2026-10-11): display precision, label spacing, off-scale arrows   [UI only] [no calculation change]
- **Display precision, no exponents:** new `latFmt(x, d)` (rounds to d decimals with `toFixed`, never exponent notation, a value that rounds to zero shows as 0, no "−0"). Used for every number the F26 code writes (labels, legends, hovers, strips, report strips) and for the F-1 hover texts of `LpileProfilePlot` (`y=`, `M=`, `V=`; before `fmt`, which switches to exponent notation below 1e-3). Toe deflection: 3 decimals like y₀. Before → after, micropile defaults: toe "−3.2227e-11 in" → "0.000 in"; H-pile defaults: "2.3615e-5 in" → "0.000 in"; hover "y=-8.0366e-4 in" → "y=-0.0008 in". Values of normal size are unchanged (e.g. 53.4 kip·ft, 3.162 in). Exception: the moment–curvature hovers keep scientific notation for the curvature φ (1/in, e.g. 2.50e-6), which is its natural unit form (pre-existing, not a label).
- **Labels spaced:** elevation labels at least 20 px apart (was 12) with the text 18 px right of the cap edge (was 8) on a white backing, so "top of bond", "plunge", "casing tip", "embed" and the cap no longer touch; casing label shortened to "(corr. …, dotted)". F-1 panel labels at least 15 px apart (was 12) and kept above the off-scale arrows. When the F26 overlay is drawn, the F25 large-deflection warning line keeps its dotted line but its label moves to the legend ("±0.25 × D = ±1.75 in (large-deflection warning)"; "(warning)" on a narrow card) instead of the vertical text on the plot, which crowded the service-limit line (`LpileProfilePlot`: `annotations: [...(EX ? [] : dwAnns), …` plus a legend-only trace; `LatProfileOne`: the warning annotation filtered out of `anns` in the F26 branch, legend-only trace added). Without the overlay (LPILE import profiles) F25's label is unchanged.
- **Off-scale capacity lines drawn as arrows:** a capacity line more than 4 × the response is still listed in the strip and now also shows as a red arrow at the right edge of its panel, bottom up: "φMn = 537.8 kip·ft → off scale", "φVn = 224.7 kip → off scale" (narrow card: "φMn→", "φVn→"); a service limit outside the deflection range shows "service limit ±1.00 in: not reached" the same way (hidden on a narrow card; in the strip).
- **Checked:** the value assertions of part b repeated for the six cases, 0 fails; no label, legend, hover (apart from the curvature φ) or strip text in exponent notation (scanned in the rendered charts, micropile and H-pile, 1500 and 400 px); parity with origin/main unchanged (report text only additions); screenshots at 1500 / 400 px and the printed pages looked at; no console errors.
- **Re-applying by hand:** unified diff below, against the merge commit `a9fcfdd` (CRLF stripped).
