## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/abut-pile-handoff-2 (ABPX2: integral demand with DW at γDW and η; CTDOT weak axis; group spacing in the load direction; drag load; tabulated AISC HP properties; engineer decisions 2026-10-20 after ABPX; PR link added after merge)

Cross-tool connection (CLAUDE.md §7 exception): the same PR changes `abutment_calculator.html` (fixlog/abutment_calculator.md ABPX2: Σx'y' in its pile distribution, drag load per pile sent) and HANDOFF.md §4.6.

### ABPX2-1. Integral mode: DW at γDW and the load modifier η   [calc change] [MORE accurate; unchanged for a project without DW / η]
- **Where:** `computeAll`, integral block (anchor `const DL = I.iabDL || 0, LL = I.iabLL || 0;`); new inputs `iabDW` (0), `iabGammaDW` (1.50), `iabEta` (1.0) in `DEFAULT_INPUTS`; integral panel (three new fields; the P_u line), report line "Factored gravity demand (Strength I)", the Module Calc "Factored gravity demand", report inputs (DW, γDW, η rows when used); hand-off `planIab` (sets `iabDL` = DC, `iabDW` = DW, `iabGammaDW`, `iabEta`; states both demands).
- **Before:** P_u = γDC·DL + γLL·LL. DW was entered inside DL at γDC, and η was not available.
- **After:** P_u = η·(γDC·DC + γDW·DW + γLL·LL). DC is in the existing DL field, DW is per pile, and η = ηD·ηR·ηI. When DW = 0 and η = 1, the old expression is evaluated, so projects saved before keep their results to the bit (checked).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 3.4.1-2 (γDC max 1.25, γDW max 1.50); Eq. 1.3.2.1-2 (η = ηD·ηR·ηI ≥ 0.95 for maximum loads); MassDOT Bridge Manual Part I §3.10.11.4 (factored gravity load per pile; the owner manual's edition per its own front matter). η is taken from the hand-off when the abutment sends one, else 1.0.
- **Check case:**
  - Inputs: integral MassDOT, skew 15°, default abutment, 6 HP12X84.
  - From the abutment: DC = 717.90/6 = 119.65 kip, DW = 72.00/6 = 12.00 kip, LL = 52.632 kip, η = 1.00.
  - Before: 1.25 × 131.65 + 1.75 × 52.632 = **256.668 kip**, D/C 0.6039.
  - After: 1.00 × [1.25(119.65) + 1.50(12.00) + 1.75(52.632)] = 149.5625 + 18.000 + 92.106 = **259.668 kip**, D/C 259.668/425 = 0.6110. This equals the abutment's P_g.
  - CTDOT, skew 10°: 290.063 kip in both tools.

### ABPX2-2. Hand-off, integral: CTDOT → weak-axis bending   [input mapping]
- **Where:** `planIab` (anchor `G.owner==='CTDOT'`).
- **Before:** web parallel to the abutment at a skew mapped to `biaxial` for every owner.
- **After:** owner CTDOT → `weak` (consistent with the CTDOT preset and its closed-form method). Other owners: weak at a skew → `biaxial`, as before; strong → `strong`.
- **Check:** CTDOT, skew 10°: `iabOrient` = weak (was biaxial). AASHTO, skew 10°: biaxial.

### ABPX2-3. Hand-off, group target: c/c spacing in the lateral-load direction   [input mapping]
- **Where:** `adoptedLayout` (new `sX`, `sY`), `plan()` group adoption (anchor `the direction of the lateral load`).
- **Why it is directional:** this tool's group effects are directional. The p-multipliers are by row in the load direction (`pmRowDir`, `pmRowsDirX`; AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 10.7.2.4, Table 10.7.2.4-1), and the trailing rows are counted along the load. There is one spacing input (`groupSpacingIn`), so it is set to the c/c spacing along the axis with the larger Σ|V| of the imported cases. When the other direction's spacing differs, the dialog says whether a case loading along the other axis is then conservative or not.
- **Before:** the smallest row / column spacing.
- **After:** the spacing along the lateral load.
- **Check:** default 3 × 8 layout, Vx dominant: s = 4.25 ft = **51 in** along x (y spacing 66 in). This is the same value as before; for this project the smallest spacing is along x.

### ABPX2-4. H-pile: drag load at the neutral plane   [calc change] [new check; MORE conservative when DR > 0; none when DR = 0]
- **Where:** `computeAll`, H-pile structural block (anchor `const DRin =`), `hs.drag`; `structPass` (anchor `(!hs.drag || hs.drag.pass)`); result rows (Structural axial at the neutral plane), the dashboard rows, report row, Module 03 (Calc + check), Pile Section panel (Drag load DR, γDR structural); hand-off `planDrag` (sets `hpDR` / `hpGammaDR` from `pileDesign.DR` / `gDR`, group target with the section adopted and per-pile target).
- **Before:** there was no drag load in this tool.
- **After:** when DR > 0, a compression case (STL > 0) that is not an Extreme Event case is checked with φc·P_o ≥ STL + γDR·DR. P_o = F_y·A_eff, with no column reduction, because the neutral plane is below the ground where the soil braces the pile. The geotechnical checks keep STL (γDR = 0.00 for geotechnical strength). The head axial / buckling and the combined checks are unchanged, since the drag load peaks at the neutral plane, not at the head.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Art. 3.11.8 (downdrag / drag load) and the note to Table 3.4.1-1 on γDR (structural strength 1.10, geotechnical 0.00), as #351 in the abutment; Art. 6.9.4.1 (P_o); 6.5.4.2 (φc).
- **Check case:**
  - Inputs: abutment default pile project with DR = 50 kip. Strength I per-pile row: STL = 212.713 kip; HP12X53 with tabulated A.
  - Demand: P_u = 212.713 + 1.10 × 50 = **267.713 kip**.
  - Resistance: A_eff = 15.5 − 4(6 − 0.97781 × 6)(0.435) = 15.268 in², P_o = 50 × 15.268 = 763.40 kip, φc·P_o = 0.60 × 763.40 = **458.04 kip** ≥ 267.71: passes.
  - An Extreme Event case has no drag check. With DR = 0 nothing changes (checked).

### ABPX2-5. H-pile: tabulated AISC properties for a rolled HP shape   [calc change] [MORE accurate; opt-in per project]
- **Where:**
  - new `HP_AISC` table (22 HP shapes, AISC Steel Construction Manual 15th Ed. database, the values of Section Property Calculator.html, checked row by row) and `hpAiscRow`;
  - `hpileSection` takes `shape`; the 9 nominal-section calls pass `shape: I.hpShape`. The corroded section stays computed;
  - new input `hpShape` (""); Pile Section panel selector "Rolled section", which fills d, b_f, t_f, t_w;
  - the section derivation, with a note on the tabulated values used, and the three-rectangle derivation kept for reference;
  - the hand-off section adoption sets `hpShape`.
- **Before:** A, I, S, Z, r from three rectangles (no fillets).
- **After:** when `hpShape` is set and d, b_f, t_f, t_w equal its table row, the checks and the p-y stiffness use the tabulated A, I_x, Z_x, S_x, r_x, I_y, Z_y, S_y, r_y. Element slenderness stays geometric. Edited dimensions or a corroded section fall back to the computed values. `hpShape` "" (every project saved before, the default) gives results identical to before.
- **Check case, HP12X53:**

  | Property | Computed (before) | Tabulated (after) |
  |---|---|---|
  | A (in²) | 2(12)(0.435) + (11.8 − 0.87)(0.435) = 15.195 | 15.5 |
  | A_eff (in²) | 14.963 | 15.268 |
  | φc·P_o, F_y 50, φc 0.60 (kip) | 448.89 | 458.04 |
  | I_x (in⁴) | 384.6 | 393 |

### Other
- Per-pile check warning text, and the receiver header comment. HANDOFF.md §4.6 updated.
- **Saved data (§5):** additive. New optional inputs `iabDW`, `iabGammaDW`, `iabEta`, `hpShape`, `hpDR`, `hpGammaDR`. Their defaults reproduce the earlier results, so no migration is needed. No key changed.
- **How verified:** `node tests/check-syntax.mjs "Pile Designer.html" abutment_calculator.html`: pass. End-to-end in jsdom 24 (React 18.2), script e2e2.js, 21 checks, all pass:
  - against origin/main `f9f3617`: default page text identical, and `computeAll` for default / H-pile / integral inputs identical (after removing the new null / default keys);
  - an integral project saved before keeps 256.668 kip;
  - the unsymmetrical layout matches the abutment for all 28 cases (worst 5.1 × 10⁻⁴ kip);
  - integral demand 259.668 = abutment; CTDOT weak; AASHTO biaxial;
  - spacing along x = 51 in; hpShape / DR / γDR set on import;
  - drag check 267.713 ≤ 458.04 with A = 15.5; no drag check in Extreme Event; the check is shown on screen.
- **Open items:**
  - The drag check uses the tool's first-pass A_eff (`hpileAeff`), as the other H-pile axial checks do. The abutment's pile structural check uses the 6.9.4.2.2 effective-width equations, so the two tools' A_eff for a slender HP flange differ slightly (HP12X53: 15.27 here vs the abutment's Tab 4 §4.4a value).
  - A corroded section uses computed properties (not tabulated minus loss).

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/pile-hp-aeff (HPAE: H-pile slender elements by the full effective-width method of 6.9.4.2.2, as the abutment calculator; engineer decision 2026-10-20 after ABPX2; PR link added after merge)

### HPAE. H-pile axial resistance: unified effective width / effective area (6.9.4.2.2) instead of the first-pass b_e   [calc change] [LESS conservative for a slender flange; unchanged for a nonslender section]
- **Where:**
  - `hpileAeff(hp, Es, Fy, Fcr)` (anchor `function hpileAeff(hp, Es, Fy, Fcr) {`), rewritten.
  - New `hpColPn(hp, Es, Fy, Pe)`.
  - `HP_AISC` rows get the AISC h/t_w (index 13), and `hpileSection` sets `web_htw` from it for a tabulated shape.
  - `computeAll`: the Module 10 column (`bklPo = F_y·A_g`, `bklHp`; `colChk` uses `hpColPn`; result `uni`) and the H-pile block (`aeDet`).
  - Pcrit ramp closure (`Pn_pcr`); report and Module 05 recomputation with the ramp.
  - Module 03 effective-area derivation (flange / web b_e worked, A_eff substituted) and Module 10 displays (the F_cr·A_eff step when a section is slender at F_cr).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Art. 6.9.4.2.2a (Eqs. 6.9.4.2.2a-1, -2, -3), 6.9.4.2.2b (Eqs. 6.9.4.2.2b-1, -2, -4; Table 6.9.4.2.2b-1), and Table 6.9.4.2.1-1. Verified against the 10th Ed. text, pp. 6-141 to 6-144 (Eq. 6.9.4.2.2b-2 read from the rendered page). Coefficients used:

  | Element | b | λ_r | c₁ | c₂ | c₃ |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Flange (supported along one edge) | b_f/2 | 0.56√(E/F_y) | 0.22 | 1.49 | 0 |
  | Web of a rolled I | h (AISC h/t_w × t_w for a tabulated shape, d − 2t_f otherwise) | 1.49√(E/F_y) | 0.18 | 1.31 | 0 |

- **Before:**
  - b_e = (λ_r/λ)·b for λ > λ_r, A_eff = max(A_g − Σ(b − b_e)t, 0.5A_g).
  - Column: P_n from the column curve with P_o = F_y·A_eff.
- **After:**
  - An element is slender when b/t > λ_r√(F_y/F_cr).
  - F_el = (c₂λ_r/(b/t))²F_y.
  - b_e = b[(1 − c₁√(F_el/F_cr))√(F_el/F_cr) − c₃].
  - A_eff = A_g − Σ(b − b_e)t.
  - Soil-braced pile (Module 03, the drag check): F_cr = F_y, P_n = P_o = F_y·A_eff.
  - Column (Module 10, all three methods and the ramp): P_cr from Eq. 6.9.4.1.1-1/-2 with P_o = F_y·A_g, F_cr = P_cr/A_g, P_n = F_cr·A_eff(F_cr). When the section is nonslender at F_cr, P_n = P_cr.
  - The corroded section stays on computed (three-rectangle) properties, with the same method.
- **Hand check, HP12X53 (tabulated A = 15.5 in², b_f = 12, t_f = t_w = 0.435 in, F_y = 50 ksi, φc = 0.60):**
  - Slenderness: b/t = 6/0.435 = 13.7931 > λ_r = 0.56√(29000/50) = 13.4866 → slender at F_cr = F_y.
  - F_el = (1.49 × 13.4866/13.7931)² × 50 = 1.45689² × 50 = 106.126 ksi; √(F_el/F_y) = 1.45689.
  - b_e = 6[(1 − 0.22 × 1.45689)(1.45689)] = 6(0.67948)(1.45689) = 5.93960 in.
  - Web: h/t_w = 22.3 ≤ 1.49√580 = 35.88 → nonslender.
  - A_eff = 15.5 − 4(6 − 5.93960)(0.435) = 15.5 − 0.10510 = **15.3949 in²** (before 15.2680).
  - P_o = 50 × 15.3949 = 769.745 kip; φc·P_o = **461.847 kip** (before 458.04).
  - **Matches the abutment calculator** (default pile project, HP12X53, Tab 4 §4.4a): A_eff = 15.3949 in², P_n = 769.745 kip, P_r = 0.60 × 769.745 = 461.847 kip. Identical to 10⁻⁹ in Pile Designer after the per-pile import, for both the axial check and the drag check (DR 50 kip: 267.713 ≤ 461.847 kip).
  - Custom (three rectangles) HP12X53: A = 15.1945 in²; A_eff 14.9625 → 15.0895 in²; φc·P_n 448.88 → 452.68 kip.
  - Column, Davisson, L_u = 15 ft:
    - P_e = 346.9 kip; P_o = F_y·A_g = 775.0 kip; P_cr = 0.658^(775.0/346.9) × 775.0 = 304.19 kip.
    - F_cr = 304.19/15.5 = 19.625 ksi; limit λ_r√(F_y/F_cr) = 21.53 > 13.79 → nonslender, so P_n = 304.19 kip.
    - Before: 303.86 kip, with P_o = F_y·A_eff = 763.4 kip.
- **Unchanged:** the default project and every H-pile section that is nonslender at F_y (the default custom H-pile, b/t = 11.95). `computeAll` is identical to origin/main `cc6fd83` for the default, H-pile, H-pile with buckling (L_u 12 ft) and integral inputs (after removing the new display keys `aeDet` / `uni`). The default page text is identical. The micropile, CFST and integral paths do not use these functions.
- **Saved data (§5):** none (no input added or changed).
- **How verified:**
  - `node tests/check-syntax.mjs "Pile Designer.html"`: pass.
  - jsdom 24 script e2e3.js: 7 checks, all pass. It covers the invariance above, the hand check, the abutment comparison (send from the abutment, per-pile import, `computeAll` on the Strength I row) and the column hand check.
- **Other copies:** the abutment calculator's `pileStructural` (abutment_calculator.html, ABCHK) uses the same equations for F_cr = F_y. It is not changed here.
- **Open items:** none.

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/aashto10-pile-rev-a (PDA, part A: AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. review fixes D1, D2, D3, D12, D5, D4 — the unconservative items of the 2026-10-20 review; engineer direction "accuracy, not extra conservatism"; PR link added after merge)

Basis: AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 10th Ed. (2024); MassDOT Bridge Manual Part I (Hundredth Anniversary Ed.) for the integral-abutment rules. Every factor and equation below was checked against the 10th Ed. text. Saved data: new optional fields only (`pdaRev`, `scourDepth`, `hpSptBasis`, `iabKb`, `iabScourCheck`, `iabCheckGammaLL`); no key or format change. `mergeSavedInputs` runs a one-time migration for a project saved without `pdaRev` (see "Saved data" at the end of this entry).

### PDA-D1. H-pile column buckling about the weak axis; Davisson depth to fixity with I_w   [calc change] [more conservative]
- **Provision:** 10th Ed. 10.7.3.13.4 (effective length = unsupported length + depth to fixity); Eqs. C10.7.3.13.4-1 / -2 (depth to fixity 1.4 (E_p I_w / E_s)^0.25 clay, 1.8 (E_p I_w / n_h)^0.2 sand, I_w = weak-axis inertia); 6.9.4.1.1 / 6.9.4.1.2 (column curve, P_e with the KL/r of the axis); 6.9.3 (KL/r <= 120).
- **Problem:** Module 10 used the bending-axis inertia and radius of gyration (`hpAxis`, default strong): `bklI = _strong ? Ix : Iy`, `bklR = _strong ? rx : ry`. An H-pile over the unsupported length is unbraced about both axes, so the weak axis (larger KL/r) governs the column; Davisson's depth to fixity is defined with I_w.
- **Where:** `computeAll`, buckling block. Anchors: `bklIw = _hp.Iy; bklRw = _hpR.ry;`, `const EI_dav = bklIw != null`, `const colChk = (Lf, PeOverride, rr) =>`, `const m_davisson = colChk(Lf_davisson, null,`, `const hpWeakChk =`, `const withWeak = m =>`, `withWeak(colChk(Lf_defl))`, `m_pcrit = withWeak(m_pcrit);`, `rampGov:`. Displays: `BucklingTabs` (Davisson characteristic length with EI_w; closer "H-pile · weak axis"), report Module 10 ("Weak-axis EI_w" input row, "H-pile: both axes unbraced", ramp-only forms gated by `r.buckling.rampGov`), H-pile Modules 03 / 05 and the report 03–09 (a P-crit override keeps a governing weak-axis result: `r.buckling.weakGov ? hs.Pn_axial :`).
- **Change:** Davisson T / R use E I_w (H-pile); the Davisson column uses r_y. The deflection-matched and P-crit methods still run in the bending plane; when that is the strong axis, the weak-axis Davisson check is also made and the lower φ_c P_n governs (`weakGov`). A manual L_f override uses r_y. Micropile: unchanged.
- **Check case (HP14×89 tabulated: A 26.1, I_x 904, I_y 326, r_x 5.88, r_y 3.53 in; F_y 50; stickup 10 ft; K 2.1; sand n_h 60 kip/ft³; strong-axis bending; Davisson):**
  - Before: T = (29000·904/144/60)^0.2 = 4.971 ft, L_f = 8.947 ft; KL = 2.1(18.947) = 39.79 ft; KL/r_x = 81.20; P_e = π²(29000)(26.1)/81.20² = 1133 kip; P_o/P_e = 1.152; P_cr = 0.658^1.152 (1305) = 805.8 kip; P_n (HPAE, slender web at F_cr) = 782.9 kip; φ_c P_n = 0.60(782.9) = **469.8 kip**.
  - After: T = (29000·326/144/60)^0.2 = 4.053 ft, L_f = 7.296 ft; KL = 2.1(17.296) = 36.32 ft; KL/r_y = 123.5 (> 120, NG flag); P_e = 490.0 kip; P_o/P_e = 2.663 > 2.25 → P_n = 0.877(490.0) = 429.7 kip; φ_c P_n = **257.8 kip** (tool 257.83). Weak-axis bending input: same after as before (257.8).
  - Strong-axis P-crit (ramp P_cr 3000 kip): bending-plane φ_c P_n 587.9 kip, weak axis 257.8 kip → weak governs (tool `weakGov` true).

### PDA-D2. Integral abutment, Tier 2 with scour: P_r with the unbraced length; scour check flood axial check   [calc change] [more conservative]
- **Provision:** MassDOT Bridge Manual Part I 3.10.11.3 (scour design flood: P_r, M_r per AASHTO with an unbraced length > 0, unbraced length = exposed depth; scour check flood: axial load only, with the unbraced length) and 3.2.10.5 (unsupported length from the bottom of the cap to the scour elevation; check flood Extreme Event II with γ_LL 0.5, 1.0 for critical / essential bridges). AASHTO 10th Ed.: 10.7.3.13.4 and Eqs. C10.7.3.13.4-1 / -2 (L_f with I_w); Table C4.6.2.5-1 (K; case "rotation fixed, translation free" design value 1.2); Eqs. 6.9.4.1.1-1 / -2, 6.9.4.1.2-1; Table 3.4.1-1 (Extreme Event II: DC 1.00, LL 0.50); 6.5.5 (φ = 1.0 at the extreme event); 1.3.3–1.3.5 (η = 1.00 outside Strength).
- **Problem:** `const Pr = phi_c * sect.Fy * sect.Ag;` with scour too (only θ_i dropped to 1.0); no check-flood check.
- **Where:** new `function iabColumn(sect, soil, Lu_ft, K)` (after `IAB_SECTIONS`); `computeAll` IAB Tier 2, anchors `const colScour = hasScour ?`, `const checkFlood = scourCk > 0 ?`, `R.iab.pass = R.iab.pass && t2_pass && (!checkFlood`; new display component `IabColumnCalcs`; Module 12 (status, "Scour design flood" calcs, heading 3a "Scour check flood"); report Module 12 lines; Tier-2 inputs "K (scour column)", "Check-flood scour (ft)", "γLL check flood".
- **Change:** with scour depth d_s > 0: L = d_s + L_f, L_f by Davisson with I_w and the MassDOT soil (sand n_h = k pci × 1.728 kip/ft³; clay E_s = 0.465 S_u ksi × 144, S_u = c), K = `iabKb` (default 1.2), KL/r_y, P_n by the column curve with P_o = F_y A_g; P_r = 0.70 P_n. Check flood (input depth > 0): P_u = DC + DW + γ_LL LL ≤ 1.0 P_n (with the check-flood depth) and KL/r ≤ 120. No scour: unchanged.
- **Check case (HP12×84: A 24.6, I_y 213, r_y 2.94; MassDOT soil 2 wet loose sand, k 20 pci; scour 8 ft; DL 120, LL 60 kip; δ_T from L 100 ft, ΔT 150 °F, weak axis; M_uy 37.2 kip-ft, M_ry 216.25 kip-ft, θ_i 1.0):**
  - Before: P_r = 0.70(50)(24.6) = **861 kip**; interaction = 255/861 + (8/9)(37.2/216.25) = 0.296 + 0.153 = **0.449**.
  - After: EI_w = 29000(213)/144 = 42,896 kip-ft²; n_h = 20(1.728) = 34.56 kip/ft³; T = (42,896/34.56)^0.2 = 4.157 ft; L_f = 7.482 ft; KL/r_y = 1.2(8 + 7.482)(12)/2.94 = 75.83; P_e = π²(29000)(24.6)/75.83² = 1224.4 kip; P_o/P_e = 1230/1224.4 = 1.005; P_n = 0.658^1.005 (1230) = 807.8 kip; P_r = 0.70(807.8) = **565.5 kip**; interaction = 255/565.5 + 0.153 = **0.604** (tool 565.46 / 0.6039).
  - Check flood 12 ft, γ_LL 0.5: P_u = 120 + 0 + 0.5(60) = 150 kip; KL/r_y = 1.2(19.482)(12)/2.94 = 95.42; P_e = 773.2 kip; P_n = 0.658^1.591 (1230) = 632.1 kip ≥ 150 → OK (before: not checked).

### PDA-D3. Micropile structural tension: φ_t 0.80; cased and uncased lengths   [calc change] [more conservative]
- **Provision:** 10.9.3.10.1 (structural resistance factors per Table 10.5.5.2.5-2); Table 10.5.5.2.5-2 (tension φ_TC = φ_TU = 0.80); 10.9.3.10.3 (cased and uncased lengths each carry the full factored tension unless the plunge transfer is used); Eq. 10.9.3.10.3a-2 (R_n = f_y (A_b + A_ct), f_y = the lesser of bar and casing); Eq. 10.9.3.10.3b-2 (R_n = f_y A_b, bar).
- **Problem:** default `phiT: 0.90` (and presets 0.95 / 0.80 from 6.5.4.2); one combined tension resistance φ_t (f_yb A_b + e_j f_yc A_cas), so with the casing counted (e_j > 0) the uncased length (bar alone) was never checked and the casing used its own f_yc.
- **Where:** `DEFAULT_INPUTS.phiT`; `PHI_PRESETS.tension`, `PHI_INFO.phiT`; `computeAll` anchors `const fyT_cas = casJointEff > 0`, `const Tn_cased =`, `const Pn_tension_cased =`, `const strUp_pass = phiPn_tension_cased >= Tu && phiPn_tension >= Tu;`; displays Module 03 "Structural tensile resistance", Module 09 "Structural tension", report Module 09.
- **Change:** φ_t default 0.80. Cased length φ_t f_y (A_b + e_j A_cas) with f_y = min(f_yb, f_yc) when the casing is counted (f_yb when e_j = 0, i.e. A_ct = 0: the bar alone); uncased length φ_t f_yb A_b; both ≥ T_u; the reported resistance is the lesser.
- **Check case 1 (defaults: A_b 0.79 in², f_yb 75 ksi, e_j 0):** T_n = 75(0.79) = 59.25 kip. Before φT_n = 0.90(59.25) = **53.3 kip** (T_u 50 passes); after 0.80(59.25) = **47.4 kip** (T_u 50 fails).
- **Check case 2 (e_j 50 %, f_yb 120, f_yc 80, A_cas 7.955 in² corroded):** before 0.90(120·0.79 + 0.5·80·7.955) = **371.7 kip**; after cased 0.80(80)(0.79 + 0.5·7.955) = 305.1 kip, uncased 0.80(120)(0.79) = 75.8 kip → **75.8 kip** governs.

### PDA-D12. Design scour depth input: no side, bond or p-y resistance above it   [calc change] [more conservative when scour > 0; default 0 = unchanged]
- **Provision:** 10.7.3.6 (the soil above the scour depth gives no axial or lateral resistance); 10.7.3.13.4 (unsupported length).
- **Problem:** scour entered only as the Module 10 "added unsupported length" (p-y soil removed only with Module 10 on); the H-pile static side resistance, the micropile bond and the p-y model kept the scoured soil.
- **Where:** new input `scourDepth` (Pile Geometry panel "Design scour depth", ft below grade); `hpileGeoCapacity(..., scour, nBasis)` (side from `zSoilTop = max(embedTop, scour)`, D_b below scour); `computeAll` micropile `Lb_scour` (bond between the casing tip and the scour line, from the head = stickup + scour), buckling `Lu_free = max(LuFree, stickup + scour)` (and the LPILE match `LuHere`), H-pile group classification `hpGroupAashto` zTop below scour; `buildPySetup` `unsupBelowGrade_in = max(Lu − stickup, scour)`; `solveLateral(..., scour)` (k = 0 above scour); deps arrays of the p-y hooks; displays (L_b,eff with − L_scour, Module 01 "Design scour", Module 10 L_u text, report).
- **Check case (HP14×89, box perimeter 2(13.8 + 14.7)/12 = 4.75 ft; sand N1,60 20 from 0–30 ft and 40 from 30–60 ft; toe 60 ft; SPT basis N1,60; φ 0.30):** before (scour 10 ft ignored) R_s = 0.4(4.75)(30) + 0.8(4.75)(30) = 57 + 114 = **171 kip**, φR_n 186.5 kip; after (scour 10 ft) R_s = 0.4(4.75)(20) + 114 = **152 kip**, φR_n **180.8 kip** (tip unchanged, D_b = 30 ft in layer 2). Micropile defaults with 20 ft scour: scour line 3 + 20 = 23 ft below the head; L_b,eff = 27 − 3 − (23 − 15) = **16.0 ft** (before 24.0 ft).

### PDA-D5. SPT method with N1,60 (overburden correction)   [calc change] [less conservative near the surface, more conservative at depth]
- **Provision:** Eqs. 10.7.3.8.6g-1 and -3 use N1,60 (corrected for overburden per 10.4.6.2.4); Eqs. 10.4.6.2.4-1 and -3: N1,60 = C_N N60, C_N = 0.77 log10(40/σ'_v), C_N < 2.0, σ'_v in ksf.
- **Problem:** the calculation used the entered value as N1,60 directly; the input was labelled N̄1,60 in the static table but N60 in the boring-log AI prompt, the import format and the notes.
- **Where:** new `sptSigmaV(sorted, z)`, `sptCN(sv)` (before `hpileGeoCapacity`); `hpileGeoCapacity` anchors `const nCorr = nBasis !== "N160";`, `spt = { N: N60, zMid, sv, CN, N160: CN * N60 };`, `tipSpt = { N: N60, z: toe`; new input `hpSptBasis` ("SPT values entered as": N60 | N1,60) in the soil profile static table; boring-log import sets N60; Module 01 table column and calcs "SPT overburden correction", "N1,60 at the tip"; report Module 01 lines.
- **Change:** basis N60 (new projects): N1,60 = C_N N60 with σ'_v from the layer unit weights (effective below the water table, as the p-y model uses them; top layer to grade), C_N at the mid-depth of each layer's contact length and at the toe for the tip; q_s = N1,60/50, q_p = 0.8 N1,60 D_b/D ≤ q_L = 8 (sand) or 6 (silt) N1,60. Basis N1,60: unchanged calculation.
- **Check case (profile of D12, no scour; γ 120 pcf 0–30 ft, 60 pcf 30–60 ft; basis N60):** layer 1 mid 15 ft σ'_v = 1.80 ksf, C_N = 0.77 log10(40/1.8) = 1.037, N1,60 = 20.74, q_s = 0.415 ksf, R_s1 = 59.1 kip; layer 2 mid 45 ft σ'_v = 4.50, C_N = 0.731, N1,60 = 29.2, R_s2 = 83.3 kip; toe σ'_v = 5.40, C_N = 0.670, N1,60 = 26.79, q_L = 214.3 ksf, q_p = min(0.8(26.79)(30)/1.225 = 524.8, 214.3) = 214.3 ksf, R_p = 214.3(1.409) = 301.9 kip. Before (values used as N1,60): R_s 171, R_p 450.8, φR_n **186.5 kip**; after: R_s 142.4, R_p 301.9, φR_n **133.3 kip** (tool 133.28).

### PDA-D4. H-pile tip in clay φ = 0.35   [calc change] [more conservative]
- **Provision:** Table 10.5.5.2.3-1 (10th Ed., p. 10-47): no separate clay end-bearing row; "side resistance and end bearing: clay and mixed soils", α-method 0.35.
- **Where:** `hpileGeoCapacity` `clay_tip:` fallback 0.40 → 0.35; `DEFAULT_INPUTS.hpPhiTipClay` 0.40 → 0.35; input label and report input row.
- **Check case (toe in clay S_u 2 ksf, HP14×89 box A_p = 13.8(14.7)/144 = 1.409 ft²):** R_p = 9(2)(1.409) = 25.36 kip; φR_p before 0.40 → **10.14 kip**, after 0.35 → **8.88 kip**.

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/aashto10-pile-rev-b (PDA, part B: D6 H-pile M_n and interaction form, D9 micropile f_y, D10 φ presets / labels, D11 n_h presets / units, D13 / D14 detailing, punching, S_u note; IAB scour M_r; C_N averaged over each layer; follow-up to part A #379; PR link added after merge)

Basis: AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 10th Ed. (2024); MassDOT Bridge Manual Part I (Hundredth Ed.); CTDOT BDM (02/24). Verified against the 10th Ed. text. Saved data: new optional field `iabEmbed` (default 24 in); `pdaRev` 2; a one-time migration note (see the end of this entry).

### PDA-D6. H-pile M_n per 6.12.2.2.1 / Appendix A6; interaction form by compactness   [calc change] [M_n: less conservative; Eq. -3: more conservative for noncompact flanges]
- **Provision:** 6.12.2.2.1a (weak axis: smaller of yielding and FLB; strong axis per 6.10); Eq. 6.12.2.2.1b-1 (M_p = F_y Z_y ≤ 1.6 F_y S_y); Eqs. 6.12.2.2.1c-1 to -5 (FLB, λ_pf = 0.38√(E/F_y), λ_rf = 1.0√(E/F_y)); Appendix A6 (6.10.6.2.3): A6.2.1 (compact web, R_pc = M_p/M_yc), A6.3.2 (FLB, rolled k_c = 0.76, F_yr = 0.7F_y, λ_rf = 0.95√(Ek_c/F_yr)), A6.3.3.1 / A6.3.3.2 (LTB, L_p, L_r, F_e, J), Eq. 6.10.8.2.3b-3 (r_t); 6.9.2.2.1 (Eqs. -1 / -2 only when all elements are compact for flexure per A6.2.1, A6.3.2, …; otherwise Eq. -3).
- **Problem:** `Mn_elastic = Fy * S_sel` and Eqs. 6.9.2.2.1-1 / -2 for every section.
- **Where:** new `hpMnAASHTO(sec, E, Fy, axis, Lb_in, Cb)`, `hpInteract(PuPr, sumMuMr, compact)`, `hpEqLbl` (before `hpileSectionForChecks`); `computeAll` H-pile anchors `const mnd = hpMnAASHTO(`, `const it = hpInteract(PuPr, MuMr, mnd.compact);`; `hpBiaxCombine`; report 03–09 and Module 05 P-crit overrides; Module 04 (`HpMnCalcs`, title "Structural Flexure"), Module 05 ("Interaction form"), `HpBiaxComb`; new `hpMnTxt`, `HpMnCalcs`.
- **Change:** weak axis M_n = min(M_p, FLB); strong axis M_n = min(FLB, LTB) with L_b = the Module 10 unsupported length (stickup + scour + added; 0 → no LTB), C_b = 1.0. A noncompact web (not the case for rolled HP shapes) is taken at R_pc = 1.0. Interaction: Eq. -1 / -2 when the web and flanges are compact, else Eq. -3 (uniaxial and biaxial).
- **Check case (HP14×89 tabulated: S_x 131, Z_x 146, S_y 44.3, Z_y 67.7, b_f/2t_f = 11.95; F_y 50; E 29000):**
  - Strong axis, L_b = 0: before M_n = 50(131) = 6550 kip-in = **545.8 kip-ft**. After: R_pc = 7300/6550 = 1.1145; λ_pf = 9.152, λ_rf = 0.95√(29000·0.76/35) = 23.84; M_nc = [1 − (1 − 35·131/7300)(11.95 − 9.152)/(23.84 − 9.152)]·7300 = **6782 kip-in = 565.2 kip-ft**.
  - Weak axis: before 50(44.3) = 2215 kip-in; after M_p = min(3385, 3544) = 3385; FLB = 3385 − (3385 − 1550.5)(2.799/14.93) = **3041 kip-in** (253.4 kip-ft).
  - Strong axis, L_b = 40 ft: r_t = 3.970 in, J = 3.194 in⁴, L_p = 105.2 in, L_r = 475.3 in; F_e = 34.52 ksi; M_n = 34.52(131) = **4522 kip-in**.
  - Interaction (P_u 300, P_r 0.70·1305 = 913.5, M_u 300 kip-ft): before Eq. -2: 0.328 + (8/9)(300/545.8) = **0.817**; after (flange noncompact → Eq. -3): 0.328 + 300/565.2 = **0.859**.

### PDA-D2b. IAB Tier 2 with scour: M_ry, M_rx per AASHTO (strong axis LTB over the scour depth)   [calc change]
- **Provision:** MassDOT 3.10.11.3 (with scour, M_rx, M_ry per AASHTO with the unbraced length); 6.12.2.2.1; Appendix A6 as D6.
- **Where:** `computeAll` IAB Tier 2, anchor `const mnScourY = hasScour ?`; Module 12 and report lines.
- **Change:** with scour, M_ry = `hpMnAASHTO(…,"weak")`, M_rx = `hpMnAASHTO(…,"strong", L_b = scour)`, φ_f = 1.00. No scour: Z ≤ 1.5S (MassDOT) unchanged.
- **Check case (part A IAB case, biaxial at 20° skew, scour 8 ft, HP12×84):** before M_ry = min(53.2, 1.5·34.6)·50/12 = 216.25, M_rx = min(120, 159)·50/12 = 500.0 kip-ft, interaction **0.6404**; after M_ry = 2660/12 = 221.67 (compact flange, M_p = min(2660, 2768)), M_rx: L_b = 96 in > L_p = 87.7 in, L_r = 459.4 in → 5949 kip-in = 495.75 kip-ft; interaction **0.6372**.

### PDA-D9. Micropile f_y: limited to the stress at 0.003 strain; uncased length uses the bar f_y   [calc change]
- **Provision:** Eq. 10.9.3.10.2a-2 (f_y = least of bar, casing and the stress at 0.003 strain); Eq. 10.9.3.10.2b-2 (bar or the stress at 0.003 strain).
- **Where:** `computeAll` anchors `const fy003 =`, `const fyU = Math.min(fyb, fy003);`, `Rn_ucased = … fyU * Ab`; Module 03 and report derivations.
- **Check cases:** (a) f_yb 120, f_yc 80: uncased f_y 80 → 87; R_n,u = 0.85[0.85(4)(37.69) + f_y(0.79)] = **162.66 → 167.36 kip**. (b) f_yb 95, f_yc 110: cased f_y 95 → 87; R_n,c = 0.85[0.85(4)(28.38) + f_y(0.79 + 7.955)] = **788.2 → 728.7 kip**. Defaults (75 / 80): unchanged.

### PDA-D10. Micropile φ presets and labels   [default change: φ_up 0.50 → 0.60]
- **Provision:** Table 10.5.5.2.5-1 (uplift: presumptive bond 0.55, preliminary only; tension load test: Table 10.5.5.2.3-1 value, ≤ 0.70); Table 10.5.5.2.3-1 (uplift, static load test 0.60); Table 10.5.5.2.5-2 (φ_CC = φ_CU = 0.75); 6.5.5 (extreme event 1.0); 10.5.5.3.2 (uplift extreme 0.80).
- **Change:** `DEFAULT_INPUTS.phiUp` 0.50 → 0.60 (tension load test, consistent with the φ_geo 0.70 load-test default); presets "tension load test 0.60" and "presumptive 0.55" (cited); φ_cc / φ_cu and extreme-event entries marked cited. Old saved 0.50 → 0.55 (migration).
- **Check case (defaults):** φ_up P_n = 0.50(109.96) = **54.98 → 0.60(109.96) = 65.97 kip**.

### PDA-D11. Sand n_h presets per Table C10.4.6.3-2; unit labels   [presets / labels only]
- **Provision:** Table C10.4.6.3-2 (ksi/ft): loose 0.417 / 0.208, medium 1.11 / 0.556, dense 2.78 / 1.39 (× 144 = kip/ft³).
- **Change:** `SAND_NH_PRESETS` 20/10, 60/35, 125/65 → 60.0/30.0, 159.8/80.1, 400.3/200.2 kip/ft³ (fills the input only; no saved result changes). Labels "pci/in" / "pci" → kip/ft³ / kip/ft² (report basis table, Module 10, lateral graph label).

### PDA-D13. Detailing per 10.7.1.2; IAB embedment   [new checks]
- **Provision:** 10.7.1.2 (spacing ≥ max(30 in, 2.5D); side of pile to cap edge ≥ 9 in; projection ≥ 12 in, 6 in with embedded bars); MassDOT 3.10.10.3 (integral piles embedded 2 ft); CTDOT BDM (piles embedded ≥ 12 in).
- **Where:** `computeAll` `embedFloor_in = isHPfix ? 12.0 : 6.0`; new `R.hpileDetail` (anchor `const det = { Dpl, embed:`), in the H-pile `fixPass`; new Module 06a "Pile Detailing"; report rows; IAB `embedChk` (input "Pile embedment into cap", default 24 in; 12 in when the Simplified tables are off, the CTDOT setting), in `R.iab.pass`.
- **Check case (HP14×89, 2×2 at 30 in, cap 6 × 6 ft, embedment 10 in):** projection 10 < 12 in NG; spacing 30 < max(30, 2.5·14.7 = 36.75) NG; edge centre 6.0 < 9 + 7.35 = 16.35 in NG. Fixed-head floor: before max(2·13.8, 6) = 27.6 in, after max(27.6, 12) = 27.6 in (the floor governs only when k·d < 12 in).

### PDA-D14. Punching 0.126λ√f'c; S_u consistency note   [calc change, +0.8 %]
- **Provision:** Eq. 5.12.8.6.3-1 (round pile β_c = 1 → the 0.126 limit; λ = 1.0 normal-weight, 5.4.2.8).
- **Check case (defaults: b_o 49.59 in, d_v 23.04 in, f'c 4 ksi):** V_n = 0.125(2)(49.59)(23.04) = **285.66 → 0.126(1.0)(2)(49.59)(23.04) = 287.95 kip**.
- S_u note: a clay layer with both the p-y s_u (psf) and the static S_u (ksf) entered and differing by more than 10 % gives an input note (no value change).

### PDA-D5b. C_N averaged over each layer's contact length   [calc change, engineer request after part A]
- **Change:** C̄_N = mean of C_N at the mid-points of n equal slices ≤ 1 ft (was C_N at the layer mid-depth); tip unchanged (C_N at the toe).
- **Check case (part A profile, basis N60):** layer 0–30 ft (γ 120 pcf): C_N(mid) 1.037 → C̄_N 1.130 (30 slices; C_N capped at 2.0 in the top 1.7 ft), R_s1 59.11 → 64.41 kip; layer 30–60 ft: 0.7306 → 0.7329, R_s2 83.29 → 83.55 kip; φR_n **133.28 → 134.95 kip**.

### Saved data
- New optional field `iabEmbed` (default 24 in). `pdaRev` 2 for new projects.
- One-time migration for a project with `pdaRev` < 2: `phiUp` 0.50 → 0.55; a load note lists the changes that apply to the project (H-pile M_n / interaction form, H-pile fixed-head floor, C̄_N, micropile f_y limits, punching, IAB scour M_r).

### How verified
- `node tests/check-syntax.mjs "Pile Designer.html"`: pass.
- jsdom harness: every check case above on origin/main `a7435f1` and the branch (tool numbers). `computeAll(DEFAULT_INPUTS)` (three pile types, micropile with Module 10): differences only φ_up (54.98 → 65.97 kip), punching (285.66 → 287.95 kip), the H-pile default M_r (537.8 → 557.0 kip-ft, Eq. -3), the fixed-head floor field, a new "embedment not entered" note and new fields. Default page text differs only in φ_up, the presets and a citation. H-pile (stickup, scour, N60) and IAB (scour, biaxial) projects load with no script errors; the part B note appears for a project with `pdaRev` 1.

### Open items
- IAB minimum / maximum spacing (MassDOT 3.10.10.3: 3'-6" to 10 ft) needs a spacing input in the IAB mode (not added).
- H-pile edge distance uses D = max(d, b_f) (the plan orientation of the web is not used).
- Strong-axis LTB uses C_b = 1.0.

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/aashto10-pile-rev-c (PDA, part C: M1 resistance determination method and R_ndr, D7 micropile group per 10.7.3.9, D8 plunge length and transfer load, IAB pile spacing, H-pile C_b input; engineer decisions "follow AASHTO"; PR link added after merge)

Basis: AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 10th Ed. (2024); RIDOT BDM (2026); CTDOT BDM (02/24); MassDOT Bridge Manual Part I (Hundredth Ed.). Verified against the texts. Saved data: new optional fields `hpResMethod` ("static"), `hpDriveOwner` ("aashto"), `hpScourBias` (1.0), `hpRsDD` (0), `hpCb` (1.0) and `hpCbMmax/MA/MB/MC` (blank), `iabSpacing` (0), `iabDetailRule` ("auto"); `pdaRev` 3 with a one-time note. No key or format change.

### PDA-M1. Driven H-pile: resistance determination method, required nominal driving resistance   [new outputs; no pass/fail change]
- **Provision:** 10.5.5.2.3 and Table 10.5.5.2.3-1 (φ_dyn: static load test + dynamic testing 0.80; static load test 0.75; dynamic testing on 100 % 0.75; dynamic testing with QC on ≥ 2 piles / 2 % 0.65; wave equation 0.50; FHWA-modified Gates 0.40; EN 0.10); C10.5.5.2.3 (the field-verification φ sets the number of piles; small groups × 0.80); 10.7.3.6 / C10.7.3.6 (R_ndr includes the side resistance lost to scour, static, unfactored, × bias); 10.7.3.7 (drag load zero at the geotechnical strength limit state); C10.7.3.3 (Eq. C10.7.3.3-1: φ_dyn R_n = φ_stat R_n,stat, the static pile-length estimate). Owner: RIDOT BDM 10.5.6 (dynamic testing on every pile-driving project, ≥ 1 production pile per substructure unit and ≥ 2 %; a static load test per site condition, which may be waived) → preset φ_dyn 0.80; CTDOT BDM (test piles with dynamic monitoring; "Ultimate Pile Capacity = factored design load / φ + scour + downdrag", φ from the geotechnical report) → preset 0.65 and the downdrag side resistance added; MassDOT: no rule beyond AASHTO.
- **Where:** new `HP_DRIVE_METHODS`; `computeAll` H-pile `const drv = (() => {` (R.hpileGeo.drv); inputs in the H-pile resistance-factor panel ("Resistance determination method", owner buttons, scour bias, CTDOT downdrag side resistance); Module 01 heading 4a "Required driving resistance"; report Module 01 line.
- **Change:** with a field method: R_n = P_u/φ_dyn (φ_dyn × 0.80 for a small group; 1.0 at the extreme event), R_ndr = R_n + λ·R_s,scour (+ R_dd for CTDOT). The static check φ_stat R_n,stat ≥ P_u (already in the tool, with the scoured soil removed) is labelled as the pile-length estimate of Eq. C10.7.3.3-1; its pass / fail does not change. Default "static": unchanged.
- **Check case (HP14×89; sand N1,60 20 / 40; toe 60 ft; scour 10 ft; P_u = 100 kip; dynamic testing with QC, φ_dyn 0.65):** R_n = 100/0.65 = **153.8 kip**; R_s,scour = 171 − 152 = 19.0 kip (λ = 1.0); R_ndr = **172.8 kip**. CTDOT with R_dd = 25 kip: R_ndr = **197.8 kip**.

### PDA-D7. Micropile group efficiency and block per 10.9.3.6 → 10.7.3.9   [calc change] [sand: less conservative; clay block: different basis]
- **Provision:** 10.9.3.6 (micropile groups per 10.7.3.9); 10.7.3.9 (cohesionless η = 1.0, no block check; cohesive: η reduced only with the cap not in firm contact over soft surface soil, 0.65 at 2.5B to 1.0 at 6B; block R_g = (2X + 2Y) Z S̄_u + X Y N_c S_u,base, Eqs. C10.7.3.9-1 to -3); Table 10.5.5.2.5-1 (block failure, clay φ_bl 0.60).
- **Before:** FHWA NHI-05-039: η = 1.0 for s ≥ 3d_h, else Converse–Labarre in any soil; block = perimeter × bond × L_b at φ_geo (0.70), in any soil.
- **Where:** `computeAll` after `R.group = {`, anchor `if (I.pileType !== "hpile" && I.pileType !== "iab") {` (g.aashtoMP); micropile `allPass` reads `R.group.geoGroup_pass` and `R.group.blockComputed`; Module 11 and report group sections (the AASHTO branch now shows for micropiles, with micropile wording).
- **Change:** `hpGroupAashto` on the micropile (B = d_h; Z = grade, buried head or design scour to the toe; S_u: static S_u, else the p-y s_u); block in cohesive soil only, φ 0.60.
- **Check case (3 × 3 at 17.5 in = 2.5 d_h, d_h 7 in, defaults):** sand: before η = 1 − (21.8°/90)(12/9) = **0.677**, φηP_n = 52.1 kip, block perimeter bond 840 kip; after η = **1.0**, φP_n = 86.6 kip, no block. - **Provision:** 10.9.3.10.4 (Eq. 10.9.3.10.4-1: P_t = φ π d_b α_b L_p; Eq. 10.9.3.10.4-2: P_u = Q − P_t on the uncased length); 10.9.3.10.2 and 10.9.3.10.3 (uncased length carries the load less P_t).

P_t = 0.70(4.581)(3) = 9.62 kip → uncased P_u = 86 − 9.62 = **76.38 kip** (before 86). Tension (T_u 50, φ_up 0.60): P_t = 8.25 kip, uncased demand 41.75 kip.

- **Provision:** Eq. 6.10.8.2.3b-1 (C_b = 12.5 M_max / (2.5 M_max + 3 M_A + 4 M_B + 3 M_C)); A6.3.3; doubly symmetric section (no R_m).
- **Where:** new `hpCbCalc(I)`; input group "C_b for lateral–torsional buckling" (C_b and M_max, M_A, M_B, M_C with "apply", as index.html); `const CbIn =` passed to `hpMnAASHTO`.

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/aashto10-pile-rev-d (PDA-DR: drivability per 10.7.8, hammer capability vs the EOD driving resistance, set-up / relaxation per 10.7.3.4; follow-up to part C #382; PR link added after merge)

### PDA-DR. H-pile drivability   [new checks; no change to existing results]
- **Provision (AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed., verified):** 10.7.8 (drivability analysis by wave equation; steel piles in compression and tension σ_dr ≤ 0.9 φ_da f_y, Eq. 10.7.8-1; analysis based on the maximum driving resistance needed, including soil subject to scour or downdrag); 6.5.4.2 (resistance during pile driving φ_da = 1.00; Table 10.5.5.2.3-1 refers to it); 10.7.3.4.1–.3 (set-up and relaxation; relaxation → restrike; set-up used only when verified by restrike); C10.7.3.4.3 (driving-formula φ developed for EOD and assuming set-up).
- **Driving stresses:** entered from a wave equation analysis (10.7.8 requires one). The 10th Ed. gives no simplified driving-stress estimate, and none is computed; no FHWA reference is in the project library, so no FHWA estimate is used.
- **Where:** `computeAll` H-pile, anchor `const drive = (() => {` (R.hpileGeo.drive; in the H-pile `allPass`); inputs in the resistance-method box (set-up factor f, hammer capability) and a new row (σ_dr compression, σ_dr tension, φ_da); Module 01 heading 4b "Drivability"; report Module 01 line. New optional fields `hpPhiDa` (1.00), `hpSigDrC` (0), `hpSigDrT` (0), `hpHammerR` (0), `hpSetupFactor` (1.0); 0 = not entered, no check. No migration needed.
- **Change:**
  - Stress: σ_dr,c and σ_dr,t ≤ 0.9 φ_da F_y.
  - Set-up / relaxation: f = R_restrike / R_EOD; EOD criterion R_ndr,EOD = R_ndr / f (R_ndr from part C, verified on restrike). For a driving formula (Gates, EN) R_ndr,EOD = R_ndr (EOD method).
  - Hammer: R_hammer ≥ R_ndr,EOD (only with a field method, when R_ndr exists).
- **Check case (part C case: HP14×89, F_y 50, P_u 100 kip, 10 ft scour, dynamic testing with QC φ_dyn 0.65 → R_ndr = 172.8 kip):**
  - Limit = 0.9(1.00)(50) = **45.0 ksi**; WEAP σ_c 38 ksi OK, σ_t 12 ksi OK; 47 ksi NG.
  - Set-up f = 1.3: R_ndr,EOD = 172.8 / 1.3 = **133.0 kip**; hammer 150 kip ≥ 133.0 OK.
  - Relaxation f = 0.9: R_ndr,EOD = 172.8 / 0.9 = **192.1 kip** > 150 NG.
  - Gates (φ_dyn 0.40): R_ndr = 100/0.40 + 19 = 269 kip = R_ndr,EOD (f not applied) > 150 NG.
- **How verified:** `node tests/check-syntax.mjs "Pile Designer.html"`: pass. jsdom: the check case numbers above; `computeAll(DEFAULT_INPUTS)` for the three pile types differs from origin/main `e7532b8` only by the new `hpileGeo.drive` object (no inputs → no checks); the H-pile project with the inputs renders Module 01 4b and the report line with no script errors.
- **Open items:** minimum penetration (10.7.6) as a driving-resistance case; blow-count limits (C10.7.8) are not checked.

Diff (`Pile Designer.html`, `git diff -U0` against origin/main `e7532b8`):
